# Rex lab v1: research, engine and page

2026-10-09 03:52:36 UTC to 2026-10-09 04:20:58 UTC. 6 assistant events, 16 subagent events, 49 tool call events, 1 user events.

The first request: a physics simulator for an indestructible plush dinosaur at strengths from the strongest human to infinite. A research workflow gathered and verified the data; the physics engine, the tests and the page were built; the owner named him Rex and went to bed.

### Owner · 2026-10-09 03:52:36 UTC

```text
Help me build a super strength simulator. I’ve got a dinosaur character (here in marketable plush form). Assuming he’s totally indestructible and inexhaustible, I want to have him do physics simulations of famous feats of strength. The goal is to understand the physics of how much force he’d have to output. Like, if this guy was as physically strong as the strongest recorded human, or various superheroes, up to effectively infinite strength, what would the physics look like? What would he be able to lift or throw? What effect would he have on his surroundings by just moving?
```

Treat it as an unofficial upper reference.","sources":[{"title":"FitnessVolt: Engelbrecht 520 kg sumo deadlift with straps","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/colton-engelbrecht-520-kg-sumo-deadlift-lifting-straps-2026-siberian-power-show/"},{"title":"OpenPowerlifting: Colton Engelbrecht","url":"https://www.openpowerlifting.org/u/coltonengelbrecht"},{"title":"Box Life: skepticism on 1,146 lb claim","url":"https://boxlifemagazine.com/viral-deadlift-record-claim-skepticism/"}]},{"key":"silver_dollar_deadlift_wr","category":"partial_lift","label":"Silver dollar (18-inch) deadlift world record","status":"verified","value_si":580,"unit_si":"kg","display":"580 kg (1,278.7 lb)","who_when":"Rauno Heinla (Estonia), 4 Jun 2022, Silver Dollar Deadlift Estonian Championship, Viljandi, Estonia","notes":"Partial range. The bar starts about 18 in (0.457 m) off the floor, so the lift is roughly knee-to-lockout. Belt and figure-8 straps. Sources disagree on a suit: FitnessVolt says he 'seems to have used' a deadlift suit, while BarBend says t-shirt, no suit. Previous record: Ben Thompson 577.2 kg (WDC Worlds, Paisley, 7 May 2022). Sean Hayes pulled about 560 kg in Apr 2022. No 2025-2026 record above 580 kg was found. Do not compare it with full-ROM deadlifts.","sources":[{"title":"FitnessVolt: Rauno Heinla 580 kg silver dollar deadlift","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/rauno-heinla-silver-dollar-deadlift-world-record/"},{"title":"BarBend: Rauno Heinla 580 kg silver dollar deadlift","url":"https://barbend.com/news/rauno-heinla-world-record-silver-dollar-deadlift-580-kilograms/"},{"title":"Breaking Muscle: Sean Hayes silver dollar deadlift (18-inch definition)","url":"https://breakingmuscle.com/sean-hayes-silver-dollar-deadlift-world-record-1235-pounds/"}]},{"key":"hummer_tire_deadlift_wr","category":"partial_lift","label":"Hummer tire deadlift world record (elevated partial deadlift)","status":"verified","value_si":549,"unit_si":"kg","display":"549 kg (1,210 lb)","who_when":"Oleksii Novikov (Ukraine), 12 Aug 2022, Shaw Classic, Loveland, Colorado, USA","notes":"Partial range: the bar starts elevated, with Hummer tires as the plates. My sources gave no start height. Belt and straps; Breaking Muscle could not tell whether he wore a suit. Beat JF Caron's 545 kg (2020). No 2025-2026 record was found.","sources":[{"title":"Breaking Muscle: Novikov 1,210 lb Hummer tire deadlift","url":"https://breakingmuscle.com/oleksii-novikov-hummer-tire-deadlift-1210-pounds/"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Max Hummer tire deadlift progression","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/strongman/records/progression/max-hummer-tire-deadlift/"}]},{"key":"trap_bar_deadlift_12in_wr","category":"partial_lift","label":"Trap bar deadlift from 12 inches (joint world record)","status":"verified","value_si":514.5,"unit_si":"kg","display":"514.5 kg (1,134 lb)","who_when":"Lucas Hatton and Evan Singleton (joint), 16 Aug 2025, Strongest Man on Earth (Shaw Classic), Loveland, Colorado, USA","notes":"Partial range: trap bar starting 12 in (0.305 m) off the floor. A different bar and setup from the 511 kg record, so it does not displace that record. Sources are Wikipedia and FitnessVolt, not a sanctioning body.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Lucas Hatton","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Hatton"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: 2025 Strongest Man On Earth results","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/2025-strongest-man-on-earth-results/"}]},{"key":"back_lift_record_ernst","category":"lift_record","label":"Heaviest weight ever lifted by a human (back lift), Guinness","status":"verified","value_si":2422.18,"unit_si":"kg","display":"2,422.18 kg (5,340 lb)","who_when":"Gregg Ernst (Canada), 28 Jul 1993, South Shore Exhibition, Bridgewater, Nova Scotia","notes":"Back lift of a platform holding two cars and their drivers, performed and notarized. A back lift is a tiny-range lift: the lifter braces under a platform resting on trestles and raises it just clear, with the load spread across the back and the legs nearly straight. Guinness gives no lift height. Displacement is very small, so work done is small even though force is huge. Guinness still named Ernst as holder in April 2026. Do not treat it as a full-ROM lift.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest weight ever lifted","url":"http://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/115841-heaviest-weight-ever-lifted"},{"title":"Guinness (Apr 2026): What is the strongest part of the human body","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2026/4/what-is-the-strongest-part-of-the-human-body-these-records-might-surprise-you"}]},{"key":"back_lift_claim_anderson_1957","category":"historical_claim","label":"Paul Anderson claimed back lift","status":"disputed","value_si":2844.02,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":1846.12,"high_si":2844.02,"display":"Claimed 6,270 lb (2,844 kg); historian's reconstruction at most ~4,070 lb (1,846 kg)","who_when":"Paul Anderson (USA), claimed 12 Jun 1957, his backyard, Toccoa, Georgia","notes":"No photos, no video and no written witness accounts. Strength historian Joe Roark (Iron Game History vol. 7 no. 1, June 2001) found the safe on the platform weighed about 1,200 lb less than claimed and the 1,800 lb wooden table was implausible. His generous reconstruction is about 4,070 lb (1,846 kg). Guinness once listed it, then removed it; I did not find the year it was removed. Even the low bound is unverified.","sources":[{"title":"Joe Roark, 'Paul Anderson's June 12, 1957 Backlift', Iron Game History 7(1), 2001","url":"https://www.starkcenter.org/igh/igh-v7/igh-v7-n1/igh0701e.pdf"},{"title":"The Barbell: Most weight ever lifted","url":"https://thebarbell.com/most-weight-ever-lifted/"}]},{"key":"back_lift_claim_cyr","category":"historical_claim","label":"Louis Cyr claimed back lift","status":"claimed","value_si":1967.23,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":1874.7,"high_si":1967.23,"display":"4,337 lb (1,967 kg) per modern retellings; 4,133 lb (1,875 kg) per 1956 Guinness wording","who_when":"Louis Cyr (Canada), reported 1895 (Boston) or 1896 (Chicago)","notes":"Platform said to carry 18 men. No photos. The Canadian Encyclopedia gives Boston 1895 and 1,967 kg. Roark quotes the 1956 Guinness listing as 4,133 lb in Chicago in 1896 (back lift off trestles). The sources disagree on weight, year and city. Historical exhibition, unverified.","sources":[{"title":"The Canadian Encyclopedia: Louis Cyr","url":"https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/article/louis-cyr"},{"title":"Joe Roark, Iron Game History 7(1), 2001 (quotes 1956 Guinness entry)","url":"https://www.starkcenter.org/igh/igh-v7/igh-v7-n1/igh0701e.pdf"},{"title":"The Barbell: Most weight ever lifted","url":"https://thebarbell.com/most-weight-ever-lifted/"}]},{"key":"hip_lift_best","category":"partial_lift","label":"Heaviest hip/harness lift (carousel)","status":"claimed","value_si":1266,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":1150,"high_si":1266,"display":"1,266 kg (2,791 lb) on TV; 1,150 kg joint competition record (2012)","who_when":"Nick Best (USA), History Channel 'The Strongest Man in History' (reported July 2019); competition mark 1,150 kg shared with Mike Jenkins, Giants Live Melbourne 2012","notes":"Hip lift: load hangs from a belt or harness at the hips and is raised only a few cm by straightening the legs. The 1,266 kg lift was a TV stunt on Paul Anderson's carousel, not a sanctioned contest. Eddie Hall said one side stayed on the ground on the first try, and Best repeated it. The 1,150 kg figure is the competition record.","sources":[{"title":"FitnessVolt: Nick Best breaks hip lift record","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/nick-best-break-hip-lift-record"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Nick Best","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Best"},{"title":"The Barbell: Most weight ever lifted","url":"https://thebarbell.com/most-weight-ever-lifted/"}]},{"key":"iwf_category_reset","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"IWF bodyweight-category changes and world-record reset (2025 and 2026)","status":"verified","value_si":0.97,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.97,"high_si":0.98,"display":"New 'World Standards' = 97% (June 2025) / 98% (Aug 2026) of trend from old records","who_when":"IWF; categories effective 1 Jun 2025, revised again effective 1 Aug 2026","notes":"From 1 Jun 2025 the IWF cut to 8 categories per sex. Men: 60, 65, 71, 79, 88, 94 (first announced as 98), 110, +110 kg. All earlier records were frozen as historical. New 'World Standards' were set at about 97% of the old records (fitted with a polynomial regression), and a lifter must beat a standard by at least 1 kg to set a record. From 1 Aug 2026 (LA28 alignment) the men's categories became 60, 65, 70, 75, 85, 95, 110, +110 kg, with new standards at 98% of a trendline. The unchanged categories (men's 60, 65, 110, +110) kept their records. So the heaviest current marks (+110 kg) are post-2025 records, while Talakhadze's heavier lifts are historical. Several IWF pages returned 403 to me, so the 97% figure comes via search summaries and Weightlifting House.","sources":[{"title":"IWF: World Standards established for new IWF bodyweight categories (Jun 2025)","url":"https://iwf.sport/2025/06/26/world-standards-established-for-new-iwf-bodyweight-categories/"},{"title":"ASOIF: IWF establishes World Standards for new bodyweight categories (Aug 2026)","url":"https://www.asoif.com/news/iwf-establishes-world-standards-new-bodyweight-categories"},{"title":"IWF: World standards for the new bodyweight categories (5 Aug 2026)","url":"https://iwf.sport/2026/08/05/iwf-establishes-world-standards-for-the-new-bodyweight-categories/"},{"title":"BarBend: IWF new weightlifting categories June 2025","url":"https://barbend.com/news/iwf-new-weightlifting-categories-june-2025/"},{"title":"Wikipedia: List of world records in Olympic weightlifting","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_Olympic_weightlifting"}]},{"key":"olympic_clean_jerk_current_wr","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"Clean & jerk world record, current categories (men +110 kg)","status":"verified","value_si":261,"unit_si":"kg","display":"261 kg (575.4 lb)","who_when":"Alireza Yousefi (Iran), 17 May 2026, Asian Weightlifting Championships, Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar, India","notes":"First record above the +110 kg World Standard of 260 kg. Full range: floor to overhead, no straps or suits, belt allowed. Yousefi's 262 kg at the 2024 Worlds came under the old +109 kg category, so it is not a current world record. The +110 total record is still the 477 kg World Standard.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: List of world records in Olympic weightlifting","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_Olympic_weightlifting"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Yousefi 261 kg clean & jerk world record","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/alireza-yousefi-sets-clean-jerk-world-record-2026-asian-weightlifting-championship/"},{"title":"Indian Weightlifting Federation report","url":"https://iwlf.in/irans-alireza-yousefi-creates-new-world-asian-records-in-mens-110kg-at-asian-weightlifting-championships-2026/"}]},{"key":"olympic_snatch_current_wr","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"Snatch world record, current categories (men +110 kg)","status":"verified","value_si":219,"unit_si":"kg","display":"219 kg (482.8 lb)","who_when":"Ali Ammar Yasser (Iraq), 29 Sep 2026, Asian Games, Aichi-Nagoya, Japan","notes":"First record above the +110 kg World Standard of 218 kg. Full range: floor to overhead in one motion. He took silver: 465 kg total against Ali Davoudi's 466 kg.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: List of world records in Olympic weightlifting","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_Olympic_weightlifting"},{"title":"Shafaq News: Timing confusion denies Iraqi weightlifter Asian gold","url":"https://shafaq.com/en/sport/Timing-confusion-denies-Iraqi-weightlifter-Asian-gold"}]},{"key":"olympic_clean_jerk_heaviest_ever","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"Heaviest clean & jerk ever (historical record, 2018-2025 categories)","status":"verified","value_si":267,"unit_si":"kg","display":"267 kg (588.6 lb)","who_when":"Lasha Talakhadze (Georgia), 17 Dec 2021, IWF World Championships, Tashkent, Uzbekistan (+109 kg)","notes":"Frozen historical record after the June 2025 category reset. Same meet: 492 kg total. It passed Leonid Taranenko's 266 kg (1988). Full range, no assistive gear beyond belt and wraps.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Lasha Talakhadze","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasha_Talakhadze"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Talakhadze three world records at 2021 Worlds","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/lasha-talakhadze-records-2021-iwf-world-championships/"},{"title":"Wikipedia: List of world records in Olympic weightlifting (historical section)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_Olympic_weightlifting"}]},{"key":"olympic_snatch_heaviest_ever","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"Heaviest snatch ever (historical record, 2018-2025 categories)","status":"verified","value_si":225,"unit_si":"kg","display":"225 kg (496 lb)","who_when":"Lasha Talakhadze (Georgia), 17 Dec 2021, IWF World Championships, Tashkent, Uzbekistan (+109 kg)","notes":"Frozen historical record after the June 2025 category reset.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Lasha Talakhadze","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasha_Talakhadze"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Talakhadze three world records at 2021 Worlds","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/lasha-talakhadze-records-2021-iwf-world-championships/"}]},{"key":"log_press_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Log lift (log press) world record","status":"verified","value_si":231,"unit_si":"kg","display":"231 kg (509.26 lb)","who_when":"Cheick 'Iron Biby' Sanou (Burkina Faso), 7 Sep 2024, Strongman Open / World Log Lift Championships, Birmingham, UK","notes":"Guinness-listed. The log is cleaned from the floor and put overhead. The sources did not give rules on leg drive or jerk style. Record history: Savickas 228 kg, Biby 229 kg (2021), 230 kg (2023), 231 kg (2024). Lucas Hatton's 222.3 kg and Jack Osborn's 222 kg (2025) are lower. The 2026 World Log Lift Challenge in Glasgow is on 17 Oct 2026, after today, so recheck after that date.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest log lift (male)","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/760344-heaviest-log-lift-male"},{"title":"Wikipedia: The World Log Lift Championships","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_World_Log_Lift_Championships"},{"title":"Burkina24: Iron Biby at 2026 World Log Lift Challenge","url":"https://burkina24.com/?p=452565"}]},{"key":"atlas_stone_over_bar_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Heaviest Atlas stone over a 48-inch bar","status":"verified","value_si":286,"unit_si":"kg","display":"286 kg (630 lb) over 1.22 m bar","who_when":"Tom Stoltman (Scotland), 23 May 2020, livestreamed record attempt (World's Ultimate Strongman 'Feats of Strength'), his gym in Scotland","notes":"The stone is lifted from the floor over a 4 ft (1.219 m) bar. Exhibition attempt, not a full contest, with Zydrunas Savickas judging remotely. Previous marks: Stoltman 273 kg (Arnold, Mar 2020) and Brian Shaw 254 kg (2017). I found no single-stone Guinness record for men and nothing heavier through 2026, but the source pages are 2020-2023.","sources":[{"title":"BarBend: Tom Stoltman 286 kg Atlas stone world record","url":"https://barbend.com/news/strongman-tom-stoltman-world-record-286kg-atlas-stone/"},{"title":"LiftingStones.org: Atlas Stones records","url":"https://liftingstones.org/articles/atlas-stones"}]},{"key":"squat_raw_sleeves_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Raw squat (sleeves) all-time world record","status":"verified","value_si":490.5,"unit_si":"kg","display":"490.5 kg (1,081.4 lb)","who_when":"Devonte Lewis (USA), 12 Jun 2026, USAPL Raw Nationals, Lombard, Illinois (bodyweight about 213.5 kg, 140+ kg class)","notes":"Federation: USAPL. Belt and knee sleeves only, no wraps or suit, full depth. It passed Ray Williams' 490 kg (2019) by 0.5 kg. His 480 kg (AMP, 30 Aug 2026) and Jesus Olivares' 485 kg (4 Oct 2026, unofficial IPF record) are lower.","sources":[{"title":"OpenPowerlifting: Devonte Lewis","url":"https://www.openpowerlifting.org/u/devontelewis"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the squat world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_squat_world_record"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: All-time raw squat records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/raw-squat-men/"}]},{"key":"squat_raw_wraps_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Raw-with-knee-wraps squat all-time world record","status":"verified","value_si":525,"unit_si":"kg","display":"525 kg (1,157.4 lb)","who_when":"Vlad Alhazov (Israel/Russia), 22 Dec 2018 (BarBend says 23 Dec), WRPF Adrenaline Grand Prix, Minsk, Belarus","notes":"Federation: WRPF. Belt and elastic knee wraps. Wraps store elastic energy out of the hole, so this is assisted compared with sleeves. BarBend noted it beat the single-ply squat record of the time. Dan Bell's 505 kg (24 Apr 2021) is lower. OpenPowerlifting's table for that meet parsed inconsistently on my fetch, so the figure rests on Wikipedia, BarBend and FitnessVolt.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the squat world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_squat_world_record"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Vladislav Alhazov","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladislav_Alhazov"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Wraps squat records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/wraps-squat-men/"}]},{"key":"squat_equipped_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Equipped (multi-ply) squat, heaviest officially recorded","status":"disputed","value_si":594.66,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":592.3,"high_si":595,"display":"About 595 kg (1,311 lb)","who_when":"Nathan Baptist (USA), 6 Feb 2021, UPA Utah Kick-Off Meet, Clearfield, Utah","notes":"Multi-ply suit plus knee wraps, which is heavily assisted. Three white lights under UPA rules, but depth has been publicly disputed from video. Sources give 594.7 kg (1,311 lb) or 595 kg (OpenPowerlifting rounding). Previous: Brian Carroll 592.3 kg (Oct 2020, RPS). I found no 600 kg squat in 2025-2026, but I could not pull a current multi-ply ranking. Single-ply all-time: 544.3 kg (Rajeev Chandila, 15 Nov 2025, per FitnessVolt).","sources":[{"title":"BarBend: Nathan Baptist 1,311 lb equipped squat","url":"https://barbend.com/powerlifter-nathan-baptist-all-time-world-record-equipped-squat-1311-pounds"},{"title":"Box Life: Contested back squat world record","url":"https://boxlifemagazine.com/contested-back-squat-world-record/"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Single-ply squat records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/equipped-squat-men/"}]},{"key":"aircraft_pull_wr","category":"pull_record","label":"Heaviest aircraft pulled by one man (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":188830,"unit_si":"kg","display":"188.83 t (416,299 lb), 8.8 m in 1 min 16 s","who_when":"Rev. Kevin Fast (Canada), 17 Sep 2009, CFB Trenton, Ontario (CC-177 Globemaster III)","notes":"The load is a rolling mass, not a lift. The pulling force only has to beat rolling resistance and inertia, a small fraction of weight, and that force was not measured. The Canadian Press gave 188,694 kg. Guinness's 'Where' field says Cobourg, which conflicts with its own text saying Trenton. Guinness does not describe the rope or harness. Still listed as current.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest aircraft pulled (male)","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/heaviest-aircraft-pulled-by-a-man"},{"title":"IronMind (18 Sep 2009): New Guinness record heaviest aircraft pulled","url":"https://ironmind.com/news/New-Guinness-World-Record-Heaviest-Aircraft-Pulled-by-an-Individual"}]},{"key":"vehicle_pull_100ft_wr","category":"pull_record","label":"Heaviest vehicle pulled over 100 ft by one man (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":99060,"unit_si":"kg","display":"99,060 kg (218,389 lb) over 30.48 m","who_when":"Rev. As with the aircraft, the force needed depends on rolling resistance and was not measured.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest vehicle pulled over 100 ft (male)","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/heaviest-vehicle-pulled-over-100ft-male"}]},{"key":"house_pull_wr","category":"pull_record","label":"Heaviest house pulled by an individual (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":35900,"unit_si":"kg","display":"35.9 t (79,145 lb), 11.95 m in 1 min 1 s","who_when":"Rev. Belt and knee sleeves only, no wraps or suit, full depth. It passed Ray Williams' 490 kg (2019) by 0.5 kg. His 480 kg (AMP, 30 Aug 2026) and Jesus Olivares' 485 kg (4 Oct 2026, unofficial IPF record) are lower.","sources":[{"title":"OpenPowerlifting: Devonte Lewis","url":"https://www.openpowerlifting.org/u/devontelewis"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the squat world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_squat_world_record"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: All-time raw squat records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/raw-squat-men/"}]},{"key":"squat_raw_wraps_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Raw-with-knee-wraps squat all-time world record","status":"verified","value_si":525,"unit_si":"kg","display":"525 kg (1,157.4 lb)","who_when":"Vlad Alhazov (Israel/Russia), 22 Dec 2018 (BarBend says 23 Dec), WRPF Adrenaline Grand Prix, Minsk, Belarus","notes":"Federation: WRPF. Belt and elastic knee wraps. Wraps store elastic energy out of the hole, so this is assisted compared with sleeves. BarBend noted it beat the single-ply squat record of the time. Dan Bell's 505 kg (24 Apr 2021) is lower. OpenPowerlifting's table for that meet parsed inconsistently on my fetch, so the figure rests on Wikipedia, BarBend and FitnessVolt.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the squat world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_squat_world_record"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Vladislav Alhazov","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladislav_Alhazov"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Wraps squat records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/wraps-squat-men/"}]},{"key":"squat_equipped_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Equipped (multi-ply) squat, heaviest officially recorded","status":"disputed","value_si":594.66,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":592.3,"high_si":595,"display":"About 595 kg (1,311 lb)","who_when":"Nathan Baptist (USA), 6 Feb 2021, UPA Utah Kick-Off Meet, Clearfield, Utah","notes":"Multi-ply suit plus knee wraps, which is heavily assisted. Three white lights under UPA rules, but depth has been publicly disputed from video. Sources give 594.7 kg (1,311 lb) or 595 kg (OpenPowerlifting rounding). Previous: Brian Carroll 592.3 kg (Oct 2020, RPS). I found no 600 kg squat in 2025-2026, but I could not pull a current multi-ply ranking. Single-ply all-time: 544.3 kg (Rajeev Chandila, 15 Nov 2025, per FitnessVolt).","sources":[{"title":"BarBend: Nathan Baptist 1,311 lb equipped squat","url":"https://barbend.com/powerlifter-nathan-baptist-all-time-world-record-equipped-squat-1311-pounds"},{"title":"Box Life: Contested back squat world record","url":"https://boxlifemagazine.com/contested-back-squat-world-record/"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Single-ply squat records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/equipped-squat-men/"}]},{"key":"aircraft_pull_wr","category":"pull_record","label":"Heaviest aircraft pulled by one man (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":188830,"unit_si":"kg","display":"188.83 t (416,299 lb), 8.8 m in 1 min 16 s","who_when":"Rev. Kevin Fast (Canada), 17 Sep 2009, CFB Trenton, Ontario (CC-177 Globemaster III)","notes":"The load is a rolling mass, not a lift. The pulling force only has to beat rolling resistance and inertia, a small fraction of weight, and that force was not measured. The Canadian Press gave 188,694 kg. Guinness's 'Where' field says Cobourg, which conflicts with its own text saying Trenton. Guinness does not describe the rope or harness. Still listed as current.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest aircraft pulled (male)","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/heaviest-aircraft-pulled-by-a-man"},{"title":"IronMind (18 Sep 2009): New Guinness record heaviest aircraft pulled","url":"https://ironmind.com/news/New-Guinness-World-Record-Heaviest-Aircraft-Pulled-by-an-Individual"}]},{"key":"vehicle_pull_100ft_wr","category":"pull_record","label":"Heaviest vehicle pulled over 100 ft by one man (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":99060,"unit_si":"kg","display":"99,060 kg (218,389 lb) over 30.48 m","who_when":"Rev. Kevin Fast (Canada), 5 Jul 2017, Cobourg, Ontario","notes":"Rolling pull over a 100 ft (30.48 m) course. The Guinness page does not describe the vehicle(s), time or harness. As with the aircraft, the force needed depends on rolling resistance and was not measured.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest vehicle pulled over 100 ft (male)","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/heaviest-vehicle-pulled-over-100ft-male"}]},{"key":"house_pull_wr","category":"pull_record","label":"Heaviest house pulled by an individual (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":35900,"unit_si":"kg","display":"35.9 t (79,145 lb), 11.95 m in 1 min 1 s","who_when":"Rev. Kevin Fast (Canada), 18 Sep 2010, Cobourg, Ontario","notes":"The house was on a wheeled transport, so this is a rolling pull. Guinness adjudicated it as a Habitat for Humanity fundraiser.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest house pulled by an individual","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/heaviest-house-pulled-by-an-individual"}]},{"key":"bus_pull_upper_body","category":"pull_record","label":"Heaviest vehicle pulled using only the upper body (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":15168.13,"unit_si":"kg","display":"33,440 lb (15,168 kg) bus, 16 ft (4.88 m)","who_when":"Rev. Kevin Fast (Canada), 20 Sep 2021, West 67th St, New York City (MTA all-electric bus, on ABC 'Live with Kelly and Ryan')","notes":"He sat on the pavement and hauled hand over hand, using no leg drive. Guinness judge Michael Empric adjudicated. UPI gives 33,400 lb, a likely typo, so I used the MTA figure. No distance is given.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest road vehicle pulled by teeth","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/heaviest-road-vehicle-pulled-by-teeth"}]},{"key":"train_pull_teeth_claim","category":"pull_record","label":"Train pulled with the teeth (reported Guinness certificate)","status":"claimed","value_si":279000,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":253104.5,"high_si":283477.1,"display":"'279 tons' (unit unspecified), about 10 m","who_when":"Ashraf Mahrous 'Kabonga' (Egypt), 13 Mar 2025, Ramses station, Cairo","notes":"The AP reported a Guinness certificate for the 'heaviest rail pull using only his teeth' and a repeat pull with a shoulder strap. AP did not say which ton: metric 279,000 kg, short 253,104 kg, long 283,477 kg. I did not find the Guinness record page. It is a rail vehicle on steel rails, so rolling resistance is very low and the force needed is tiny compared with the weight.","sources":[{"title":"AP via WSLS: Egyptian wrestler pulls a train with his teeth, sets 3 world records","url":"https://www.wsls.com/entertainment/2025/03/13/he-can-pull-a-train-by-the-strength-of-his-teeth-an-egyptian-wrestler-sets-3-world-records/"}]},{"key":"weight_sustained_on_body_wr","category":"static_support","label":"Heaviest weight sustained on the body (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":2000,"unit_si":"kg","display":"2,000 kg (4,409.24 lb)","who_when":"Muli Bujar (Kosovo), 18 Jul 2026, Vushtrri, Kosovo","notes":"Static support, not a lift: 40 x 50 kg cement bags stacked on a plywood board resting on his body. A World Athletics preview in Sep 2026 confirms the record stands.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Javelin throw","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javelin_throw"},{"title":"World Athletics: Men's javelin preview, World Ultimate Championship Budapest 26","url":"https://worldathletics.org/competitions/world-athletics-ultimate-championship/2026/news/preview/preview-men-javelin-world-ultimate-championship-budapest-26"}]},{"key":"discus_wr","category":"throw_record","label":"Men's discus world record","status":"verified","value_si":75.56,"unit_si":"m","display":"75.56 m","who_when":"Mykolas Alekna (Lithuania), 13 Apr 2025, Oklahoma Throws Series World Invitational, Ramona, Oklahoma, USA","notes":"2 kg discus. It was first logged at 105.1 mph and later revised to 105.8 mph when the tracking data was standardized (SABR). Guinness credits 'Statcast, which began recording velocities in 2008', but the 2008-2014 system was PITCHf/x, so the label is loose. This is a ball speed near release, not a hand speed. Fastest since: 105.7 mph (Chapman, 2016); 105.5 mph (Ben Joyce, 2024; Jacob Misiorowski, 26-27 Jun 2026, a record for a starter). No 106+ mph pitch is on record.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Fastest baseball pitch (male)","url":"http://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/fastest-baseball-pitch-male"},{"title":"SABR Games Project: Sept 24, 2010, Chapman tops 105 mph","url":"https://sabr.org/gamesproj/game/september-24-2010-reds-aroldis-chapman-tops-105-mph-for-fastest-pitch-ever-recorded/"},{"title":"Screwball: Fastest pitches thrown in MLB 2026","url":"https://www.screwball.com/mlb/fastest-pitches-in-2026"}]},{"key":"fastest_punch_guinness_claim","category":"speed_record","label":"Fastest martial arts punch (Guinness)","status":"claimed","value_si":20.1168,"unit_si":"m/s","display":"45 mph (72.42 km/h, 20.1 m/s)","who_when":"Keith Liddell (USA), 2013 (beat his own 44 mph from 2012), Body Tac Karate Dojo, Chicago","notes":"LOW SOURCE QUALITY for physics. Guinness gives no method (sensor, camera or point on the fist). The figure is about 1.6-3x peak fist speeds measured in peer-reviewed motion capture (about 6.6-12.5 m/s), so it should not set the human ceiling in the sim. Wikipedia cites the 2013 Guinness 'Fan Choice' item.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records news (9 Aug 2013): Fan Choice Record, fastest martial arts punch","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2013/8/fan-choice-record-august-9-50361/"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Keith Liddell","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Liddell"}]},{"key":"punch_fist_speed_elite_measured","category":"biomechanics_endpoint_speed","label":"Elite punch fist speed (lab-measured)","status":"verified","value_si":11.95,"unit_si":"m/s","low_si":6.6,"high_si":12.5,"display":"Peak about 6.6-12.5 m/s; best mean peak 11.95 m/s (lead hook)","who_when":"Whiting, Gregor & Finerman 1988; Piorkowski, Lees & Barton 2011; Stanley et al. 2018","notes":"Whiting et al. 1988 (Am J Sports Med 16(2):130-136, 3D film, experienced boxers): peak fist velocity 6.6-12.5 m/s, reached 8-21 ms before contact; contact velocity 5.9-8.2 m/s. Piorkowski et al. 2011 (10 competition-standard athletes, 8-camera optoelectronic): single maximal contact speed 9.26 +/- 2.09 m/s; hooks faster than jab or cross. They also cite Atha et al. 1985: 8.9 m/s contact for one professional heavyweight (Frank Bruno), and Walilko 2005: 8.16 m/s for amateurs. Stanley et al. 2018 (IJPAS 18:835-854, 15 amateurs): lead hook peak 11.95 +/- 1.84 m/s, the highest punch type. Straight punches are slower: elite lead straight 7.16 m/s (Liu et al. 2022). Karate punches are reported at 10-15 m/s (Feld, McNair & Wilk, Sci Am 1979, via a secondary source only). Peak speed and contact speed differ.","sources":[{"title":"Whiting et al. 1988, Am J Sports Med 16(2):130-136 (record)","url":"https://lida.sport-iat.de/dbv/Record/4039170?lng=en"},{"title":"Piorkowski, Lees & Barton 2011, Single maximal versus combination punch kinematics (accepted manuscript)","url":"https://knowledge.lancashire.ac.uk/3757/1/piorkowski-et-al-2011-punch-kinematics.pdf"},{"title":"Stanley et al. 2018, IJPAS 18(5):835-854","url":"https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/rpanxx/v18y2018i5p835-854.html"},{"title":"Liu et al. 2022, Frontiers in Physiology 13:1015154","url":"https://frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fphys.2022.1015154/full"},{"title":"Science.ca Ask a Scientist (cites Sci Am April 1979 karate article)","url":"https://science.ca/askascientist/viewquestion.php?qID=821"}]},{"key":"standing_vertical_jump_nfl_record","category":"jump_record","label":"Highest standing vertical jump, NFL Scouting Combine record","status":"verified","value_si":1.1684,"unit_si":"m","display":"46 in (1.168 m)","who_when":"Gerald Sensabaugh (North Carolina), 2005 NFL Scouting Combine, Indianapolis","notes":"Measured as jump-and-reach (Vertec): standing reach subtracted from jump reach, with countermovement and arm swing. Looper says 'holds up a weight of 200 quintillion tons with one hand behind his back'. Exact panel wording and page: cannot verify. Range is short to long ton. The researcher was asked:
TOPIC: Physical data for an object library the dinosaur can lift or throw.
For each object give: mass (value_si, with low/high if it varies), typical dimensions (L x W x H in m, in notes), frontal/cross-section area estimate for a thrown object in m^2, drag coefficient estimate (state the shape assumption; note tumbling bluff bodies are ~1.0 and supersonic spheres ~0.9-1.0), the material at the grip point and its crush/yield/compressive strength in Pa (e.g., car body sheet steel, aircraft aluminium skin, granite), and a one-line structural note on what happens if you try to lift the whole thing from one hand-sized contact point.
Objects: baseball; men's shot put; max-weight bowling ball; average adult human; Steinway Model D grand piano; a typical motorcycle; Toyota Corolla curb mass; Ford F-150 curb mass; full-size Type C school bus; US semi truck at the 80,000 lb legal max; M1A2 SEPv3 Abrams tank; adult blue whale (typical and largest recorded); EMD SD70ACe locomotive; Boeing 747-400 (operating empty and max takeoff); Airbus A380 max takeoff; Space Shuttle full stack at liftoff; Statue of Liberty (copper skin + steel framework + total); Eiffel Tower (iron structure and total); RMS Titanic displacement; Nimitz-class carrier full-load displacement; Empire State Building total mass estimate (state method/uncertainty); Great Pyramid of Giza mass; Mount Everest mass estimate (state the method and the definition of where the mountain ends, give a range); a typical cumulus cloud's water mass; the Moon; Earth; the Sun.
Prefer manufacturer specs, official agencies (NASA, USGS, NPS), and reputable references. Mark rough estimates as status estimate.

For comparison, SEPv2 is 71.2 short tons (64.6 t). Dimensions (Abrams family): length 9.77 m gun forward, 7.93 m hull; width 3.66 m; height 2.44 m. Grip material: composite armour, including depleted-uranium layers on the M1A2, over steel (rolled homogeneous armour, hardness classes 260 to 470 HB, mat_rha). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~65 MPa, well under armour-steel strength. The welded hull is a stiff box, so a hull lift should hold. Most masses come from length regressions or piecemeal weighing (Lockyer 1976). NOAA Fisheries: North Atlantic/North Pacific animals reach ~90 ft (27 m) and over 100,000 lb; Antarctic animals reach ~110 ft (33.5 m) and over 330,000 lb (149.7 t). Typical length ~26 m (NOAA PMEL). Grip material: skin and blubber over muscle; tissue strength not quantified. Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~98 MPa, about half the compressive strength of cortical bone and far above any plausible soft-tissue strength. A hand would sink into the animal rather than lift it. Out of water, a whale's body is not built to carry its own weight from one point (not quantified). Other workers (Paul & Larramendi 2025) argue for lower ceilings around 200 t, so treat heavier figures as disputed models, not records. Grip stress at 1 g is ~186 MPa. Area: blue_whale_projected_area.","who_when":"Whale taken 1947; Guinness listing 2023"},{"key":"blue_whale_projected_area","category":"object_area","label":"Blue whale projected area (prolate-spheroid model)","value_si":44,"low_si":6.4,"high_si":77.6,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"~6 (nose-on) to ~56-78 m^2 (broadside)","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://pmel.noaa.gov/acoustics/whales/whale-biology-blue.html","title":"NOAA PMEL - typical length 26 m"}],"notes":"Estimate. Grip material: the external tank is aluminium-lithium 2195 (Super Lightweight Tank) under spray-on foam insulation. Absolute 2195 yield is not quantified here (NASA says ~29% higher than 2219). Copper sheeting is 3/32 in (2.38 mm) thick. Grip material: annealed-temper copper sheet (~69 MPa yield, mat_copper_annealed). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g for the whole statue (~204 t) is ~200 MPa, about 3x copper yield, so the thin skin crushes and tears. Structural note: grip stress at 1 g for the whole tower (10,100 t) is ~9.9 GPa, about 25 to 35x the iron's strength. A single-member grip just rips that member out. The tower stands on four legs on masonry foundations and must be separated from them. Height ~324 to 330 m depending on antennas; base ~125 m square. Neither was re-verified this pass.","who_when":"SETE key figures (2018 release)"},{"key":"eiffel_tower_total_mass","category":"object_mass","label":"Eiffel Tower total mass (incl. non-metal parts)","value_si":10100000,"unit_si":"kg","display":"10,100 tonnes","status":"verified","sources":[{"url":"https://sete.toureiffel.paris/sites/default/files/2018-07/Press_Release__SETE_-.pdf","title":"SETE press release - total weight 10,100 tonnes"},{"url":"https://www.lego.com/cdn/cs/set/assets/bltab6941ae7803cfea/21019_EiffelTower_A4_ENUS_v2_2_2.pdf","title":"LEGO 21019 fact sheet"}],"notes":"Each repaint uses about 60 t of paint. The 66,000 ton figure is a myth that came from early advertising. Gross register tonnage (46,328 GRT) is a volume measure, not mass. Displacement is the mass of ship plus everything aboard at that draught. Dimensions: length 882 ft 9 in (269.06 m), beam 92 ft 6 in (28.19 m), draught 34 ft 7 in (10.54 m), waterline to boat deck 60 ft 6 in (18.44 m). Grip material: riveted mild-steel hull plate (~193 MPa yield, mat_titanic_hull_steel). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~52 GPa. Even a perfect grip just tears out the plate. A ship is designed to be supported by distributed buoyancy, and out of water a single-point lift breaks the hull girder. Drag: tumbling bluff body Cd ~1.0 to 1.3.","who_when":"Harland & Wolff data, 1912"},{"key":"rms_titanic_projected_area","category":"object_area","label":"Titanic projected area (hull bounding box)","value_si":8100,"low_si":818,"high_si":7800,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"~820 (bow-on) to ~8,100 m^2","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://titanicinternationalsociety.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/titanic-fact-sheet.pdf","title":"Titanic fact sheet dimensions"}],"notes":"Box 269.06 x 28.19 x 29.0 m (keel to boat deck = draught 10.54 + 18.44; funnels excluded). The value is the midpoint, and the mass varies by hull (later ships are heavier). Naval-technology gives 102,000 t. One database lists CVN-77 at 104,208 tons full and 81,083 tons light. Dimensions: length 332.8 m overall (317.0 m waterline), flight-deck beam 76.8 m, waterline beam 40.8 m, draft 11.3 m. Grip material: high-strength hull steel. HY-80 has a 552 MPa minimum yield (mat_hy80). Wikipedia says ships from John C. Stennis onward used HSLA-100. Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~1.0e11 Pa, about 200x HY-80 yield. A single-point grip tears out plate, and lifting from water snaps the hull girder.","who_when":"Polmar 2004 via Wikipedia"},{"key":"nimitz_projected_area","category":"object_area","label":"Nimitz-class projected area (rough box)","value_si":12400,"low_si":1220,"high_si":13600,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"~1,200 (bow-on) to ~13,600 m^2 (top)","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nimitz-class_aircraft_carrier","title":"Wikipedia - Nimitz dimensions"}],"notes":"Box 332.8 x 40.8 (waterline beam) x 30 m. Exterior: 200,000 ft^3 of Indiana limestone and granite, 10 million bricks, 730 tons of aluminium and stainless steel. Height 1,454 ft (443.2 m) to antenna tip. Lot 79,288 ft^2. Grip material: Indiana limestone facade (min 4,000 psi = 27.6 MPa compressive, mat_indiana_limestone) anchored to a steel frame. The literature figure is ~6 Mt (5.5 Mt limestone + 0.5 Mt mortar + 8,000 t granite). Low bound: limestone alone, 5.5 Mt. High bound (my calculation): the full ~2.6e6 m^3 envelope at 2.67 to 2.72 t/m^3 gives ~7.0 Mt if it were solid limestone. The real figure is lower because the envelope includes a natural bedrock hillock and voids. Block counts are disputed (2.3 to ~4 million). Base 230.3 m per side; height 146.6 m originally, 138.5 m now. Grip material: limestone blocks set with mortar (UCS 6 to 245 MPa, mat_limestone_generic). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~5.9e12 Pa. The pyramid is a pile of separate blocks, so a grip pulls out one block and the rest stays.","who_when":"Literature estimates; accessed 2026-10"},{"key":"great_pyramid_projected_area","category":"object_area","label":"Great Pyramid projected area","value_si":34725,"low_si":16881,"high_si":53038,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"~16,900 (face-on) to 53,000 m^2 (top); orientation mean ~34,700 m^2","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza","title":"Wikipedia - base 230.3 m, original height 146.6 m"}],"notes":"Ideal square pyramid with the original height. Hawaii rock-properties lecture (densities, UCS)"},{"url":"https://mounteverest.info/?p=4587","title":"Popular page repeating ~357 trillion lb (1.62e14 kg), origin untraceable"}],"notes":"My own calculation. I found no peer-reviewed or survey-agency mass estimate. Method: a right circular cone, V = pi r^2 h / 3, at rock density 2,700 kg/m^3 (2,600 to 2,800 changes the result by about 4%). Summit 8,848.86 m. Definition A (central value): the mountain ends at ~5,200 m, roughly the elevation of the main base camps (not verified), so relief h = 3.65 km, and base radius r = 6 km gives V = 138 km^3 and M = 3.7e14 kg. Low (r = 4 km, same h) gives 61 km^3 and 1.65e14 kg, close to the widely repeated but unsourced 1.62e14 kg. High (base at ~4,000 m valley floors, h = 4.85 km, r = 10 km) gives 508 km^3 and 1.4e15 kg. Counting only the summit pyramid above ~7,000 m (h = 1.85 km, r = 2 km) gives just ~2e13 kg. Rock below the chosen base plane, including the crustal root, is excluded by definition. Geology: the summit is the Qomolangma Formation (Ordovician limestone) above the Yellow Band (marble/limestone, ~8,600 m), with schists and gneisses lower. UCS: limestone 6 to 245, marble 55 to 274, schist 25 to 62, gneiss 50 to 230 MPa. Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~3.6e17 Pa. 'Lifting' Everest means quarrying it free of the crust, so model it as excavation, not a grip.","who_when":"Height: China-Nepal joint survey, 8 Dec 2020; mass derived 2026-10"},{"key":"mount_everest_projected_area","category":"object_area","label":"Everest cone-model projected areas","value_si":21900000,"low_si":14600000,"high_si":113000000,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"side ~2.2e7 m^2; footprint ~1.1e8 m^2 (r = 6 km cone)","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://thehimalayantimes.com/nepal/everest-2-0-worlds-tallest-peaks-revised-height-revealed-stands-at-8848-86m/","title":"Summit height 8,848.86 m"}],"notes":"For the central cone (r = 6 km, h = 3.65 km): side silhouette r*h = 2.19e7 m^2; footprint pi r^2 = 1.13e8 m^2. The low value is the side silhouette for r = 4 km. Air drag is irrelevant at this scale compared with the mass.","who_when":"Derived"},{"key":"cumulus_cloud_water_mass","category":"object_mass","label":"Typical (1 km^3) cumulus cloud - liquid water only","value_si":500000,"unit_si":"kg","display":"~500,000 kg (~1.1 million lb) of droplets","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/how-much-does-a-cloud-weigh","title":"USGS Water Science School - How much does a cloud weigh?"},{"url":"https://www.earthdate.org/episodes/puffy-clouds-weigh-in","title":"EarthDate - Puffy clouds weigh in (same 0.5 g/m^3 assumption)"}],"notes":"USGS illustration: 1 km^3 = 1e9 m^3 x ~0.5 g/m^3 liquid water content = 5e8 g = ~500,000 kg. This counts droplets only. The air in the same volume is roughly 1e9 kg at ~1 kg/m^3 (my rough figure, not sourced). Real liquid water content and size vary widely, and the range was not sourced. Grip material: none. A cloud is suspended droplets in air with no structural strength. A 'grab' would just push air and droplets aside. Model it as moving air, not a rigid body. Cross-section: cloud_cross_section_area.","who_when":"USGS Water Science School (current)"},{"key":"cloud_cross_section_area","category":"object_area","label":"1 km x 1 km cumulus cross-section","value_si":1000000,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"~1e6 m^2","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/how-much-does-a-cloud-weigh","title":"USGS 1 km cube cloud"}],"notes":"Follows from the USGS 1 km cube assumption.","who_when":"Derived"},{"key":"moon_mass","category":"object_mass","label":"Moon","value_si":7.346e+22,"unit_si":"kg","display":"7.346e22 kg","status":"verified","sources":[{"url":"https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html","title":"NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet (updated 11 Jan 2024)"}],"notes":"Volumetric mean radius 1,737.4 km; mean density 3,344 kg/m^3; GM 4,902.8 km^3/s^2 (listed as 0.00490 x 10^6 km^3/s^2); mean Earth-Moon distance 384,400 km. Not a 'grip' object. It is a self-gravitating body, and any hand-sized contact just craters the surface. Model it as applying force over a large area or as a gravitational problem. Cross-section: moon_cross_section_area.","who_when":"NASA NSSDCA, 2024-01-11"},{"key":"moon_cross_section_area","category":"object_area","label":"Moon cross-sectional area","value_si":9483000000000,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"9.48e12 m^2","status":"verified","sources":[{"url":"https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html","title":"NASA Moon Fact Sheet (radius)"}],"notes":"pi r^2 with r = 1,737.4 km.","who_when":"Derived"},{"key":"earth_mass","category":"object_mass","label":"Earth","value_si":5.9722e+24,"unit_si":"kg","display":"5.9722e24 kg","status":"verified","sources":[{"url":"https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html","title":"NASA NSSDCA Earth Fact Sheet (updated 15 Nov 2024)"}],"notes":"Volumetric mean radius 6,371.0 km; equatorial 6,378.137 km; mean density 5,513 kg/m^3; GM 3.9860e14 m^3/s^2. Cd(M) = 0.45 M^2 + 0.424 for 0 <= M <= 0.722. For M > 0.722, Cd(M) = 2.1 exp(-1.2(M+0.35)) - 8.9 exp(-2.2(M+0.35)) + 0.92. Sample values: M 0.3 = 0.464, M 0.9 = 0.82, M 1.0 = 0.88, peak ~1.00 at M ~1.7, M 3 = 0.95, M >= 5 = 0.92. The paper's quoted low-speed value is 0.46. This fit ignores the Reynolds-number drag crisis: a smooth sphere above Re ~3e5 can drop to ~0.1 to 0.2, and NASA Glenn gives a sphere Cd range of 0.07 to 0.5. Use for the shot, bowling ball, and any compact rounded object.","who_when":"Carter et al. For M > 1.150, Cd(M) = 2.1 exp(-1.16(M+0.35)) - 6.5 exp(-2.23(M+0.35)) + 1.67. The two pieces do not join exactly at M = 1.15 (1.83 vs 1.81). The paper quotes a low-speed cube value of 1.09 and a hypersonic plateau of 1.67. Use this as the default for tumbling vehicles, pianos, tanks and buildings, with area = orientation-averaged projected area.","who_when":"Carter et al. NOAA Fisheries: North Atlantic/North Pacific animals reach ~90 ft (27 m) and over 100,000 lb; Antarctic animals reach ~110 ft (33.5 m) and over 330,000 lb (149.7 t). Typical length ~26 m (NOAA PMEL). Grip material: skin and blubber over muscle; tissue strength not quantified. Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~98 MPa, about half the compressive strength of cortical bone and far above any plausible soft-tissue strength. A hand would sink into the animal rather than lift it. Out of water, a whale's body is not built to carry its own weight from one point (not quantified). The low value is 62,000 lb (31 short tons), cited by CNN and attributed by CDA to NPS. The high value is 200,000 lb from the 2000 NPS handbook. CDA's own estimate is 179,000 lb. Copper sheeting is 3/32 in (2.38 mm) thick. Grip material: annealed-temper copper sheet (~69 MPa yield, mat_copper_annealed). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g for the whole statue (~204 t) is ~200 MPa, about 3x copper yield, so the thin skin crushes and tears. Structural note: grip stress at 1 g for the whole tower (10,100 t) is ~9.9 GPa, about 25 to 35x the iron's strength. A single-member grip just rips that member out. Dimensions: length 882 ft 9 in (269.06 m), beam 92 ft 6 in (28.19 m), draught 34 ft 7 in (10.54 m), waterline to boat deck 60 ft 6 in (18.44 m). Grip material: riveted mild-steel hull plate (~193 MPa yield, mat_titanic_hull_steel). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~52 GPa. Even a perfect grip just tears out the plate. Exterior: 200,000 ft^3 of Indiana limestone and granite, 10 million bricks, 730 tons of aluminium and stainless steel. Height 1,454 ft (443.2 m) to antenna tip. Lot 79,288 ft^2. Grip material: Indiana limestone facade (min 4,000 psi = 27.6 MPa compressive, mat_indiana_limestone) anchored to a steel frame. The literature figure is ~6 Mt (5.5 Mt limestone + 0.5 Mt mortar + 8,000 t granite). Low bound: limestone alone, 5.5 Mt. High bound (my calculation): the full ~2.6e6 m^3 envelope at 2.67 to 2.72 t/m^3 gives ~7.0 Mt if it were solid limestone. The real figure is lower because the envelope includes a natural bedrock hillock and voids. Block counts are disputed (2.3 to ~4 million). Base 230.3 m per side; height 146.6 m originally, 138.5 m now. Grip material: limestone blocks set with mortar (UCS 6 to 245 MPa, mat_limestone_generic). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~5.9e12 Pa. The pyramid is a pile of separate blocks, so a grip pulls out one block and the rest stays.","who_when":"Literature estimates; accessed 2026-10"},{"key":"great_pyramid_projected_area","category":"object_area","label":"Great Pyramid projected area","value_si":34725,"low_si":16881,"high_si":53038,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"~16,900 (face-on) to 53,000 m^2 (top); orientation mean ~34,700 m^2","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza","title":"Wikipedia - base 230.3 m, original height 146.6 m"}],"notes":"Ideal square pyramid with the original height. Hawaii rock-properties lecture (densities, UCS)"},{"url":"https://mounteverest.info/?p=4587","title":"Popular page repeating ~357 trillion lb (1.62e14 kg), origin untraceable"}],"notes":"My own calculation. I found no peer-reviewed or survey-agency mass estimate. Method: a right circular cone, V = pi r^2 h / 3, at rock density 2,700 kg/m^3 (2,600 to 2,800 changes the result by about 4%). Summit 8,848.86 m. Definition A (central value): the mountain ends at ~5,200 m, roughly the elevation of the main base camps (not verified), so relief h = 3.65 km, and base radius r = 6 km gives V = 138 km^3 and M = 3.7e14 kg. Low (r = 4 km, same h) gives 61 km^3 and 1.65e14 kg, close to the widely repeated but unsourced 1.62e14 kg. High (base at ~4,000 m valley floors, h = 4.85 km, r = 10 km) gives 508 km^3 and 1.4e15 kg. Counting only the summit pyramid above ~7,000 m (h = 1.85 km, r = 2 km) gives just ~2e13 kg. Rock below the chosen base plane, including the crustal root, is excluded by definition. Geology: the summit is the Qomolangma Formation (Ordovician limestone) above the Yellow Band (marble/limestone, ~8,600 m), with schists and gneisses lower. UCS: limestone 6 to 245, marble 55 to 274, schist 25 to 62, gneiss 50 to 230 MPa. Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~3.6e17 Pa. 'Lifting' Everest means quarrying it free of the crust, so model it as excavation, not a grip.","who_when":"Height: China-Nepal joint survey, 8 Dec 2020; mass derived 2026-10"},{"key":"mount_everest_projected_area","category":"object_area","label":"Everest cone-model projected areas","value_si":21900000,"low_si":14600000,"high_si":113000000,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"side ~2.2e7 m^2; footprint ~1.1e8 m^2 (r = 6 km cone)","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://thehimalayantimes.com/nepal/everest-2-0-worlds-tallest-peaks-revised-height-revealed-stands-at-8848-86m/","title":"Summit height 8,848.86 m"}],"notes":"For the central cone (r = 6 km, h = 3.65 km): side silhouette r*h = 2.19e7 m^2; footprint pi r^2 = 1.13e8 m^2. Air drag is irrelevant at this scale compared with the mass.","who_when":"Derived"},{"key":"cumulus_cloud_water_mass","category":"object_mass","label":"Typical (1 km^3) cumulus cloud - liquid water only","value_si":500000,"unit_si":"kg","display":"~500,000 kg (~1.1 million lb) of droplets","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/how-much-does-a-cloud-weigh","title":"USGS Water Science School - How much does a cloud weigh?"},{"url":"https://www.earthdate.org/episodes/puffy-clouds-weigh-in","title":"EarthDate - Puffy clouds weigh in (same 0.5 g/m^3 assumption)"}],"notes":"USGS illustration: 1 km^3 = 1e9 m^3 x ~0.5 g/m^3 liquid water content = 5e8 g = ~500,000 kg. This counts droplets only. The air in the same volume is roughly 1e9 kg at ~1 kg/m^3 (my rough figure, not sourced). Real liquid water content and size vary widely, and the range was not sourced. Grip material: none. A cloud is suspended droplets in air with no structural strength. A 'grab' would just push air and droplets aside. Model it as moving air, not a rigid body. Cross-section: cloud_cross_section_area.","who_when":"USGS Water Science School (current)"},{"key":"cloud_cross_section_area","category":"object_area","label":"1 km x 1 km cumulus cross-section","value_si":1000000,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"~1e6 m^2","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/how-much-does-a-cloud-weigh","title":"USGS 1 km cube cloud"}],"notes":"Follows from the USGS 1 km cube assumption.","who_when":"Derived"},{"key":"moon_mass","category":"object_mass","label":"Moon","value_si":7.346e+22,"unit_si":"kg","display":"7.346e22 kg","status":"verified","sources":[{"url":"https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html","title":"NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet (updated 11 Jan 2024)"}],"notes":"Volumetric mean radius 1,737.4 km; mean density 3,344 kg/m^3; GM 4,902.8 km^3/s^2 (listed as 0.00490 x 10^6 km^3/s^2); mean Earth-Moon distance 384,400 km. Not a 'grip' object. It is a self-gravitating body, and any hand-sized contact just craters the surface. Model it as applying force over a large area or as a gravitational problem. Cross-section: moon_cross_section_area.","who_when":"NASA NSSDCA, 2024-01-11"},{"key":"moon_cross_section_area","category":"object_area","label":"Moon cross-sectional area","value_si":9483000000000,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"9.48e12 m^2","status":"verified","sources":[{"url":"https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html","title":"NASA Moon Fact Sheet (radius)"}],"notes":"pi r^2 with r = 1,737.4 km.","who_when":"Derived"},{"key":"earth_mass","category":"object_mass","label":"Earth","value_si":5.9722e+24,"unit_si":"kg","display":"5.9722e24 kg","status":"verified","sources":[{"url":"https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html","title":"NASA NSSDCA Earth Fact Sheet (updated 15 Nov 2024)"}],"notes":"Volumetric mean radius 6,371.0 km; equatorial 6,378.137 km; mean density 5,513 kg/m^3; GM 3.9860e14 m^3/s^2. Cd(M) = 0.45 M^2 + 0.424 for 0 <= M <= 0.722. For M > 0.722, Cd(M) = 2.1 exp(-1.2(M+0.35)) - 8.9 exp(-2.2(M+0.35)) + 0.92. Sample values: M 0.3 = 0.464, M 0.9 = 0.82, M 1.0 = 0.88, peak ~1.00 at M ~1.7, M 3 = 0.95, M >= 5 = 0.92. The paper's quoted low-speed value is 0.46. This fit ignores the Reynolds-number drag crisis: a smooth sphere above Re ~3e5 can drop to ~0.1 to 0.2, and NASA Glenn gives a sphere Cd range of 0.07 to 0.5. Use for the shot, bowling ball, and any compact rounded object.","who_when":"Carter et al. (NASA NTRS 20110016614)"},{"key":"cd_cube_mach_fit","category":"drag_coefficient","label":"Cube drag coefficient vs Mach (tumbling compact bluff body)","value_si":1.09,"low_si":1.04,"high_si":1.83,"unit_si":"1","display":"~1.04-1.09 subsonic, peak ~1.83 at M 1.15, 1.67 hypersonic","status":"verified","sources":[{"url":"https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20110016614/downloads/20110016614.pdf","title":"Carter, Jandir & Kress - meteor drag (cube data to Mach 3)"}],"notes":"Cd(M) = 0.60 M^2 + 1.04 for 0 <= M <= 1.150. For M > 1.150, Cd(M) = 2.1 exp(-1.16(M+0.35)) - 6.5 exp(-2.23(M+0.35)) + 1.67. The two pieces do not join exactly at M = 1.15 (1.83 vs 1.81). The paper quotes a low-speed cube value of 1.09 and a hypersonic plateau of 1.67. Use this as the default for tumbling vehicles, pianos, tanks and buildings, with area = orientation-averaged projected area.","who_when":"Carter et al. (NASA NTRS 20110016614)"},{"key":"cd_baseball_subsonic","category":"drag_coefficient","label":"Baseball drag coefficient (game speeds)","value_si":0.35,"low_si":0.3,"high_si":0.6,"unit_si":"1","display":"~0.35 in play (wind-tunnel 0.3 to 0.6)","status":"claimed","sources":[{"url":"https://mdpi-res.com/d_attachment/applsci/applsci-12-01416/article_deploy/applsci-12-01416.pdf","title":"Smith & Sciacchitano 2022, Applied Sciences 12:1416 (non-spinning MLB ball 0.3-0.6; in play ~0.35)"},{"url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/0712.0380","title":"Influence of a humidor on the aerodynamics of baseballs (drag crisis discussion)"}],"notes":"The seams trigger an early drag crisis, and Cd depends on speed and spin. Coarse well-graded material at Dr 80-100% reaches 44-46 deg (Table 3-1a). c' = 0.","who_when":"USACE 1992"},{"key":"ground_dense_sand_gravel_claw_traction_coefficient","category":"ground_dense_sand_gravel","label":"Dense sand / gravel: effective traction coefficient for a clawed foot","status":"estimate","value_si":0.84,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.7,"high_si":1,"display":"~0.84 (0.7-1.0)","sources":[{"title":"Basis: friction angles from USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Table 3-1","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"}],"notes":"My estimate, using the same reasoning as for loose sand: claws engage the granular layer, so the limit is about tan(phi') = 0.73-1.0 for 36-45 deg. BGS lists BS 5930 'Soft' as UCS 0.04-0.08 MPa, i.e. s_u = UCS/2 = 20-40 kPa. ISO 14688-2 and BS 5930:2015 call 20-40 kPa 'low'. The US-style scale (labelled ASTM D-2488 in the groundhog docs; Terzaghi & Peck in origin) puts 'soft' at 12.5-25 kPa. The central 20 kPa is my choice. Use undrained strength for rapid stomps. Very soft clay is below 12.5-20 kPa.","who_when":"BS 5930 / ISO 14688-2 / Terzaghi & Peck consistency scales"},{"key":"ground_soft_clay_ultimate_bearing_small_footing","category":"ground_soft_clay","label":"Soft clay: ultimate (undrained) bearing capacity, square foot at the surface","status":"estimate","value_si":128600,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":77000,"high_si":296000,"display":"q_ult ~ 6.2-7.4 x s_u ~ 129 kPa (77-296 kPa)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Tables 4-1, 4-2, 4-4 (Nc = 5.14 Prandtl / 5.7 Terzaghi; Terzaghi square factor 1.3)","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"},{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-2908 Rock Foundations, Table 6-1 (Sowers 1979 shape corrections: square 1.25, circular 1.2)","url":"https://www.cedengineering.com/userfiles/Rock%20Foundations-R1.pdf"}],"notes":"phi = 0 analysis: q_ult = N_c * shape * s_u (+ gamma*D). The factor ranges from 5.14 x 1.2 = 6.17 to Terzaghi's 5.7 x 1.3 = 7.41. The central value uses 5.14 x 1.25 = 6.43 with s_u = 20 kPa. Undrained capacity does NOT depend on foot size, unlike sand. Low end: 6.17 x 12.5 kPa. High end: 7.41 x 40 kPa.","who_when":"Derived 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_soft_clay_presumptive_allowable","category":"ground_soft_clay","label":"Soft clay: presumptive ALLOWABLE bearing pressure","status":"verified","value_si":47880,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":47880,"high_si":71820,"display":"NAVFAC/USACE soft inorganic clay 1 ksf (47.9 kPa); IBC Class 5 clay/silt 1,500 psf (71.8 kPa, any consistency)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Table 4-8","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"},{"title":"IBC/CBC Table 1806.2 (reproduction)","url":"https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/ca-building-code/chapter-18-soils-and-foundations/section-1806-presumptive-load-bearing-values-of-soils"}],"notes":"ALLOWABLE values. Under rapid (undrained) loading, the horizontal force the ground can resist at the sole is about s_u x A and does NOT grow with the normal load. For s_u = 12.5-40 kPa and A = 0.1 m^2 that is 1.25-4 kN, plus passive resistance on buried claws and toes. The engine should cap traction at min(mu*N, s_u*A + passive). The mu range covers a wet, smeared clay surface.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_stiff_clay_undrained_shear_strength","category":"ground_stiff_clay","label":"Stiff clay: undrained shear strength s_u","status":"verified","value_si":75000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":50000,"high_si":150000,"display":"s_u ~ 50-100 kPa (US scale 'stiff') or 75-150 kPa (BS 5930:1999 'stiff'; ISO 'high')","sources":[{"title":"BGS OR/15/065 Appendix 2 (BS 5930: Stiff = UCS 0.15-0.3 MPa)","url":"https://earthwise.bgs.ac.uk/index.php/OR/15/065_Appendix_2_-_Strength,_consistency_and_density_classification_terms_and_descriptions"},{"title":"Geocentrix: ISO 14688-2","url":"https://www.geocentrix.co.uk/help/content/references/iso14688/undrained_shear_strength_of_fine_soils.htm"},{"title":"Groundhog docs: strength bands","url":"https://groundhog.readthedocs.io/en/dev/site_investigation/categories.html"}],"notes":"The central 75 kPa (where the two schemes overlap) is my choice. Same undrained traction-cap logic as for soft clay.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_asphalt_allowable_contact_pressure_aviation","category":"ground_asphalt","label":"Asphalt (flexible) pavement: allowable tyre-pressure categories in the pavement rating system","status":"verified","value_si":1750000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":500000,"display":"W unlimited; X <= 1.75 MPa (254 psi); Y <= 1.25 MPa (181 psi); Z <= 0.50 MPa (73 psi)","sources":[{"title":"Fiji CAA AIC 04/25 (ICAO ACR-PCR tyre pressure codes)","url":"https://caaf.org.fj/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/AIC-04-25-CHANGES-TO-PAVEMENT-STRENGTH-CLASSIFICATION-SYSTEM.pdf"},{"title":"Iowa DOT PCR report 2024 (FAA AC 150/5335-5D codes)","url":"https://ia.iowadot.gov/aviation/pavementmanagement/airport-details/docs/pcr-reports/fort-dodge-pcr-report-2024.pdf"}],"notes":"These are serviceability limits for repeated aircraft tyre loads on rated airfield pavements. They are not the ultimate capacity under a single static punch. Ordinary roads are not rated this way. Code W has no limit, so no high_si is given. The value shown is the X limit.","who_when":"ICAO ACR-PCR / FAA AC 150/5335-5D"},{"key":"ground_asphalt_ultimate_bearing_small_punch","category":"ground_asphalt","label":"Asphalt pavement on compacted base: ultimate bearing under a 0.1 m^2 foot","status":"estimate","value_si":2500000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":1000000,"high_si":5000000,"display":"~1-5 MPa (order-of-magnitude estimate)","sources":[{"title":"Context only: tyre-pressure categories (Fiji CAA AIC 04/25)","url":"https://caaf.org.fj/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/AIC-04-25-CHANGES-TO-PAVEMENT-STRENGTH-CLASSIFICATION-SYSTEM.pdf"}],"notes":"Order-of-magnitude estimate only. I found no published ultimate static punch capacity. Reasoning: high-category flexible pavements routinely carry tyre pressures up to 1.75 MPa in service without damage, so the single-load ultimate is higher. The asphalt and base spread the load onto the subgrade, which ultimately governs. Asphalt is viscoelastic, so it is much weaker when hot and under sustained load (rutting) than when cold and under rapid load. Treat the range as very uncertain.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_asphalt_claw_traction_coefficient","category":"ground_asphalt","label":"Asphalt: friction coefficient, keratin scales/claws","status":"estimate","value_si":0.7,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.5,"high_si":0.9,"display":"~0.7 (0.5-0.9) dry","sources":[{"title":"No direct source found (estimate)","url":"https://what-if.xkcd.com/1/"}],"notes":"My estimate; no measured data found. The URL is a placeholder because the schema requires one; it does not support this number. Reasoning: dry asphalt's coarse macrotexture lets claw tips interlock with aggregate, giving roughly rubber-like grip. Wet surfaces would be lower. With very high force, claws plough the binder and the limit becomes asphalt shear failure, for which I found no value.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_concrete_slab_fc","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Concrete slab-on-grade: specified compressive strength f'c","status":"verified","value_si":24130000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":17240000,"high_si":27580000,"display":"17.2 MPa (2,500 psi) interior slabs; 20.7-24.1 MPa (3,000-3,500 psi) exposed garage slabs; 27.6 MPa (4,000 psi) steel-troweled garage option","sources":[{"title":"Minnesota Rules 1309.0402 (IRC Table R402.2 as amended), 2019 version","url":"https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/1309.0402/version/2019-11-13%2011:38:17+00:00"}],"notes":"These are residential minimums (IRC Table R402.2 as adopted in Minnesota). Industrial floors commonly specify higher strengths, but I did not verify a typical industrial value, so high_si stops at 4,000 psi. 1 psi = 6,894.757 Pa.","who_when":"IRC R402.2 (MN-amended, 2019)"},{"key":"ground_concrete_bearing_strength_aci","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Concrete local bearing (crushing) strength per ACI 318","status":"verified","value_si":41000000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":14650000,"high_si":46900000,"display":"B_n = 0.85 f'c A1 sqrt(A2/A1), sqrt(A2/A1) <= 2 (max 1.7 f'c); phi = 0.65","sources":[{"title":"Lecture (ACI 318 bearing check, phi = 0.65, sqrt(A2/A1) <= 2)","url":"https://www.uomus.edu.iq/img/lectures21/MUCLecture_2022_8556371.pdf"}],"notes":"A1 is the loaded area and A2 the geometrically similar supporting area. A foot on a large slab gets the full sqrt(A2/A1) = 2. Value: 1.7 x 24.13 MPa = 41 MPa. Low: 0.85 x 17.24 MPa (no confinement benefit). High: 1.7 x 27.58 MPa. This is a code nominal limit; actual crushing under a confined punch can be higher. In practice the slab punches through or cracks in flexure well before the surface crushes (see next entries). The secondary source cites the ACI 318 bearing clause; I could not open the code text.","who_when":"ACI 318 bearing provisions"},{"key":"ground_concrete_punching_shear_stress_aci","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Concrete two-way (punching) shear stress capacity, ACI 318","status":"verified","value_si":1620000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":1370000,"high_si":1730000,"display":"v_c = 4 lambda sqrt(f'c) psi = 0.33 lambda sqrt(f'c) MPa (smallest of three ACI expressions); critical perimeter b0 at d/2 from the loaded area","sources":[{"title":"StructurePoint: GammaF in two-way slab punching shear (ACI 318-14)","url":"https://structurepoint.org/publication/pdf/The%20Role%20of%20GammaF%20in%20Two-way%20Slab%20Punching%20Shear%20Calculations%20in%20ACI%20318.pdf"}],"notes":"v_c = min(4, 2 + 4/beta, alpha_s*d/b0 + 2) x lambda*sqrt(f'c) psi. Values computed for f'c = 17.24-27.58 MPa (central 24.13 MPa). This is for structural two-way slabs. Plain slabs-on-ground are designed differently (ACI 360, not checked), and subgrade support inside the perimeter adds capacity.","who_when":"ACI 318-14 two-way shear provisions"},{"key":"ground_concrete_slab_on_grade_punch_through_estimate","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Slab-on-grade: average foot pressure to punch through (0.1 m^2 foot)","status":"estimate","value_si":2500000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":2300000,"high_si":8000000,"display":"~2.5 MPa (100 mm residential slab) to ~8 MPa (200 mm, 34 MPa slab)","sources":[{"title":"Formula basis: ACI 318 two-way shear (StructurePoint)","url":"https://structurepoint.org/publication/pdf/The%20Role%20of%20GammaF%20in%20Two-way%20Slab%20Punching%20Shear%20Calculations%20in%20ACI%20318.pdf"}],"notes":"My calculation: V = 0.33*sqrt(f'c)*b0*d, with b0 = 4(B + d), B = 0.316 m and d taken as the slab thickness. Cases: 100 mm at 17-21 MPa gives V ~ 0.23-0.25 MN (about 2.3-2.5 MPa under the foot). 150 mm at 27.6 MPa gives ~0.48 MN. 200 mm at 34.5 MPa gives ~0.80 MN. Caveats: this ignores subgrade reaction (which raises capacity), plain-concrete and reinforcement effects, and flexural cracking (which may come first). After cracking the slab acts as broken plates on the subgrade.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_concrete_claw_traction_coefficient","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Concrete: friction coefficient, keratin scales/claws","status":"estimate","value_si":0.6,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.4,"high_si":0.8,"display":"~0.6 (0.4 smooth/troweled to 0.8 broom-finished)","sources":[{"title":"Context: IBC Table 1806.2 friction coefficients (concrete footing on soil/rock)","url":"https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/ca-building-code/chapter-18-soils-and-foundations/section-1806-presumptive-load-bearing-values-of-soils"}],"notes":"My estimate; no measured data found. Keratin cannot penetrate concrete, so this is surface friction plus claw-tip catching on texture. Steel-troweled slabs are at the low end, broom-finished at the high end.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_granite_ucs","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Intact granite: uniaxial compressive strength (UCS)","status":"verified","value_si":200000000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":100000000,"high_si":300000000,"display":"~100-250+ MPa; fresh granite is an ISRM 'extremely strong' (>250 MPa) example","sources":[{"title":"Hoek, Practical Rock Engineering, Ch. 11, Table 2 (field estimates of UCS)","url":"https://www.rocscience.com/assets/resources/learning/hoek/Practical-Rock-Engineering-Chapter-11-Rock-Mass-Properties.pdf"},{"title":"BGS OR/15/065 Appendix 2 (rock strength classes)","url":"https://earthwise.bgs.ac.uk/index.php/OR/15/065_Appendix_2_-_Strength,_consistency_and_density_classification_terms_and_descriptions"}],"notes":"Hoek's Table 2 classes are R5 Very strong 100-250 MPa (examples include granodiorite and gneiss) and R6 Extremely strong >250 MPa (examples include fresh granite and quartzite). Hoek gives m_i = 32 +/- 3 for granite. Weathered granite is far weaker. The 200 MPa central value and the 300 MPa high end are my choices; 300 MPa is not a hard ceiling.","who_when":"Hoek (Practical Rock Engineering); Brown 1981 grades"},{"key":"ground_granite_bearing_confinement_factor","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Rock under a small punch: ultimate bearing / UCS (confinement factor)","status":"estimate","value_si":8.5,"unit_si":"1","low_si":1,"high_si":13.8,"display":"q_ult ~ (N_phi + 1) x UCS (strip) x 1.25 (square); N_phi = tan^2(45 + phi/2) -> ~8.5-14 for intact rock; lower bound ~1 x UCS","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-2908 Rock Foundations (1994), Eqs 6-2, 6-4, 6-5, 6-7 and Table 6-1","url":"https://www.cedengineering.com/userfiles/Rock%20Foundations-R1.pdf"}],"notes":"Derivation from the EM 1110-1-2908 equations: local-shear q_ult = c*N_c (+ 0.5*gamma*B*N_gamma), with N_c = 2*N_phi^0.5*(N_phi + 1). For intact rock the lower-bound cohesion is c = q_u/(2*tan(45 + phi/2)) (Eq 6-7a, s = 1). Together these give q_ult ~ q_u*(N_phi + 1) for a strip, times 1.25 for a square (Sowers). For an assumed intact friction angle phi = 45-55 deg, N_phi = 5.8-10.1, so the factor is 6.8-11.1 (strip) or 8.5-13.8 (square). The phi range is my assumption, not sourced. Poorly confined, jointed rock columns fail near the unconfined strength (Eq 6-5: 2c*tan(45 + phi/2) = q_u), so the factor drops toward 1. Secondary sources attribute q_ult = q_u(N_phi + 1) to Goodman (1989); I did not open Goodman.","who_when":"Estimate built on USACE EM 1110-1-2908 (30 Nov 1994)"},{"key":"ground_granite_ultimate_bearing_small_punch","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Intact granite: ultimate bearing under a 0.1 m^2 foot","status":"estimate","value_si":1700000000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":100000000,"high_si":4100000000,"display":"~1.7 GPa (0.1-4 GPa)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-2908","url":"https://www.cedengineering.com/userfiles/Rock%20Foundations-R1.pdf"},{"title":"Hoek Ch. 11","url":"https://www.rocscience.com/assets/resources/learning/hoek/Practical-Rock-Engineering-Chapter-11-Rock-Mass-Properties.pdf"}],"notes":"UCS x confinement factor: 200 MPa x 8.5 = 1.7 GPa. Low: jointed or weathered rock at about its UCS (100 MPa x 1). High: 300 MPa x 13.8. Real outcrops are jointed, and the joints often govern.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_granite_presumptive_allowable","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Crystalline bedrock (granite): presumptive ALLOWABLE bearing","status":"verified","value_si":7660800,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":574560,"high_si":7660800,"display":"NAVFAC/USACE massive crystalline rock, hard sound: 160 ksf (7.66 MPa); IBC Class 1 crystalline bedrock 12,000 psf (575 kPa)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Table 4-8","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"},{"title":"IBC/CBC Table 1806.2","url":"https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/ca-building-code/chapter-18-soils-and-foundations/section-1806-presumptive-load-bearing-values-of-soils"}],"notes":"ALLOWABLE values. These are 200-3,000 times below the estimated ultimate for an intact punch because they cover jointing, settlement and safety factors.","who_when":"Dept. of the Navy 1982 via USACE 1992; ICC IBC"},{"key":"ground_granite_intact_cohesion_estimate","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Intact granite: Mohr-Coulomb cohesion (shear strength intercept)","status":"estimate","value_si":36000000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":16000000,"high_si":62000000,"display":"c ~ q_u / (2 tan(45 + phi/2)) ~ 0.16-0.21 x UCS ~ 36 MPa","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-2908 Eq 6-7a","url":"https://www.cedengineering.com/userfiles/Rock%20Foundations-R1.pdf"}],"notes":"Computed for UCS = 100-300 MPa and assumed phi = 45-55 deg. Shear strength is tau = c + sigma*tan(phi).","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_granite_claw_traction_coefficient","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Granite: friction coefficient, keratin scales/claws","status":"estimate","value_si":0.5,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.3,"high_si":0.7,"display":"~0.5 (0.3 polished to 0.7 rough outcrop)","sources":[{"title":"Context: IBC Table 1806.2 (crystalline bedrock sliding coefficient 0.70 for concrete footings)","url":"https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/ca-building-code/chapter-18-soils-and-foundations/section-1806-presumptive-load-bearing-values-of-soils"}],"notes":"My estimate; no measured data found. Keratin is far softer than quartz and feldspar, so claws cannot bite into intact granite. Grip comes from surface roughness only.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_ibc_sliding_coefficients","category":"ground_general","label":"IBC lateral sliding resistance (concrete footing on soil/rock), for context","status":"verified","low_si":0.25,"high_si":0.7,"unit_si":"1","display":"Crystalline bedrock 0.70; sedimentary rock 0.35; sandy gravel 0.35; sand/silty sand 0.25; clay: cohesion 130 psf (6.22 kPa) x contact area","sources":[{"title":"IBC/CBC Table 1806.2 and footnotes","url":"https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/ca-building-code/chapter-18-soils-and-foundations/section-1806-presumptive-load-bearing-values-of-soils"}],"notes":"Design (allowable) values for concrete footings, not keratin. The coefficient multiplies the dead load. Clay sliding resistance is cohesion x area, capped at half the dead load (section 1806.3.2).","who_when":"ICC IBC"},{"key":"ground_steel_a36_yield","category":"ground_steel_plate","label":"Structural steel plate ASTM A36: minimum yield strength","status":"verified","value_si":250000000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":220000000,"high_si":250000000,"display":"36 ksi (248-250 MPa); 32 ksi (220 MPa) for plates thicker than 8 in","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: A36 steel (citing AISC Steel Construction Manual)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A36_steel"}],"notes":"Secondary source; ASTM and AISC pages were blocked (403). 36 ksi converts to 248.2 MPa; ASTM A36M uses 250 MPa. The range covers the 142-149 g rule limits.","who_when":"Munroe 2012 (scenario); energy derived 2026-10"},{"key":"seismic_gutenberg_richter_energy_magnitude","category":"seismic","label":"Gutenberg-Richter energy-magnitude relation","status":"verified","unit_si":"J","display":"log10 E_s = 1.5 M + 4.8 (E_s in J)  ==  log10 E_s = 1.5 M_s + 11.8 (E_s in erg)","sources":[{"title":"Collins, Melosh & Marcus (2005) Meteoritics & Planetary Science 40(6):817-840, Eq. 40 ('classic Gutenberg-Richter magnitude energy relation', citing Melosh 1989 p. 67)","url":"https://impact.ese.ic.ac.uk/static/effects.pdf"}],"notes":"Original: Gutenberg & Richter (1956), Annali di Geofisica 9:1-15, which I did not open.
