The limit is then about mu_eff ~ tan(phi') = 0.53-0.62 for phi' = 28-32 deg. Passive resistance in front of buried toes and claws can add somewhat. A very hard push excavates the sand instead of moving the dinosaur.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_dense_sand_gravel_ultimate_bearing_small_footing","category":"ground_dense_sand_gravel","label":"Dense sand / gravel: ultimate bearing capacity, 0.1 m^2 square foot at the surface","status":"estimate","value_si":241000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":118000,"high_si":650000,"display":"~240 kPa (range ~120-650 kPa)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-1905, Tables 3-1, 4-1, 4-2","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"}],"notes":"My calculation. Terzaghi surface square footing: q_ult = 0.5*gamma*B*N_gamma*0.8 with B = 0.316 m. Low end: phi' = 36 deg, gamma = 18 kN/m^3 (N_gamma = 52.0). Central: phi' = 40 deg, gamma = 19 kN/m^3 (N_gamma = 100.4). High end: very dense gravel, phi' = 44 deg, gamma = 20 kN/m^3 (N_gamma = 257). The result is very sensitive to phi' and grows linearly with foot width. Any embedment adds the gamma*D*N_q term, which is large: N_q = 81 at 40 deg.","who_when":"Derived 2026-10 from USACE 1992"},{"key":"ground_dense_sand_gravel_presumptive_allowable","category":"ground_dense_sand_gravel","label":"Dense sand / gravel: presumptive ALLOWABLE bearing pressure","status":"verified","value_si":383040,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":143640,"high_si":670320,"display":"NAVFAC/USACE: very compact coarse-medium sand 8 ksf (383 kPa); very compact gravel 14 ksf (670 kPa). IBC Class 3 sandy gravel 3,000 psf (143.6 kPa)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-1905, Table 4-8 (Dept. of the Navy 1982)","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"},{"title":"IBC/CBC Table 1806.2 (reproduction)","url":"https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/ca-building-code/chapter-18-soils-and-foundations/section-1806-presumptive-load-bearing-values-of-soils"}],"notes":"ALLOWABLE values. The NAVFAC/USACE gravel entries are 6 ksf loose, 10 ksf medium-compact and 14 ksf very compact. Coarse-medium sand is 3, 6 and 8 ksf. For footings under 3 ft wide, multiply by B(ft)/3, about 0.35 for a 0.1 m^2 foot.","who_when":"Dept. of the Navy 1982 via USACE 1992; ICC IBC"},{"key":"ground_dense_sand_gravel_friction_angle","category":"ground_dense_sand_gravel","label":"Dense sand / gravel: effective friction angle (tau = sigma' tan phi')","status":"verified","value_si":0.6981,"unit_si":"rad","low_si":0.6283,"high_si":0.7854,"display":"phi' ~ 40 deg (36-45 deg); tan phi' ~ 0.73-1.0","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-1905, Table 3-1a (Schmertmann 1978) and 3-1b","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"}],"notes":"Dense sand (Dr 60-80%, N60 30-50) is 38-41 deg (Meyerhof 1974), 36-41 deg (Peck, Hanson & Thornburn) or 40-45 deg (Meyerhof cone correlation). Very dense is above 41 deg. Coarse well-graded material at Dr 80-100% reaches 44-46 deg (Table 3-1a). c' = 0.","who_when":"USACE 1992"},{"key":"ground_dense_sand_gravel_claw_traction_coefficient","category":"ground_dense_sand_gravel","label":"Dense sand / gravel: effective traction coefficient for a clawed foot","status":"estimate","value_si":0.84,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.7,"high_si":1,"display":"~0.84 (0.7-1.0)","sources":[{"title":"Basis: friction angles from USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Table 3-1","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"}],"notes":"My estimate, using the same reasoning as for loose sand: claws engage the granular layer, so the limit is about tan(phi') = 0.73-1.0 for 36-45 deg. BGS lists BS 5930 'Soft' as UCS 0.04-0.08 MPa, i.e. s_u = UCS/2 = 20-40 kPa. ISO 14688-2 and BS 5930:2015 call 20-40 kPa 'low'. The US-style scale (labelled ASTM D-2488 in the groundhog docs; Terzaghi & Peck in origin) puts 'soft' at 12.5-25 kPa. The central 20 kPa is my choice. Use undrained strength for rapid stomps. Very soft clay is below 12.5-20 kPa.","who_when":"BS 5930 / ISO 14688-2 / Terzaghi & Peck consistency scales"},{"key":"ground_soft_clay_ultimate_bearing_small_footing","category":"ground_soft_clay","label":"Soft clay: ultimate (undrained) bearing capacity, square foot at the surface","status":"estimate","value_si":128600,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":77000,"high_si":296000,"display":"q_ult ~ 6.2-7.4 x s_u ~ 129 kPa (77-296 kPa)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Tables 4-1, 4-2, 4-4 (Nc = 5.14 Prandtl / 5.7 Terzaghi; Terzaghi square factor 1.3)","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"},{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-2908 Rock Foundations, Table 6-1 (Sowers 1979 shape corrections: square 1.25, circular 1.2)","url":"https://www.cedengineering.com/userfiles/Rock%20Foundations-R1.pdf"}],"notes":"phi = 0 analysis: q_ult = N_c * shape * s_u (+ gamma*D). The factor ranges from 5.14 x 1.2 = 6.17 to Terzaghi's 5.7 x 1.3 = 7.41. The central value uses 5.14 x 1.25 = 6.43 with s_u = 20 kPa. Undrained capacity does NOT depend on foot size, unlike sand. Low end: 6.17 x 12.5 kPa. High end: 7.41 x 40 kPa.","who_when":"Derived 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_soft_clay_presumptive_allowable","category":"ground_soft_clay","label":"Soft clay: presumptive ALLOWABLE bearing pressure","status":"verified","value_si":47880,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":47880,"high_si":71820,"display":"NAVFAC/USACE soft inorganic clay 1 ksf (47.9 kPa); IBC Class 5 clay/silt 1,500 psf (71.8 kPa, any consistency)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Table 4-8","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"},{"title":"IBC/CBC Table 1806.2 (reproduction)","url":"https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/ca-building-code/chapter-18-soils-and-foundations/section-1806-presumptive-load-bearing-values-of-soils"}],"notes":"ALLOWABLE values. The IBC table does not separate clay by consistency and excludes organic clays, peat and mud.","who_when":"Dept. of the Navy 1982 via USACE 1992; ICC IBC"},{"key":"ground_soft_clay_traction","category":"ground_soft_clay","label":"Soft clay: traction for a clawed foot","status":"estimate","value_si":0.25,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.1,"high_si":0.4,"display":"effective mu ~0.1-0.4; or traction cap ~ s_u x contact area (1.25-4 kN per 0.1 m^2 foot)","sources":[{"title":"Basis: s_u bands (BGS / ISO 14688-2)","url":"https://earthwise.bgs.ac.uk/index.php/OR/15/065_Appendix_2_-_Strength,_consistency_and_density_classification_terms_and_descriptions"}],"notes":"My estimate; no measured data found. Under rapid (undrained) loading, the horizontal force the ground can resist at the sole is about s_u x A and does NOT grow with the normal load. For s_u = 12.5-40 kPa and A = 0.1 m^2 that is 1.25-4 kN, plus passive resistance on buried claws and toes. The engine should cap traction at min(mu*N, s_u*A + passive). The mu range covers a wet, smeared clay surface.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_stiff_clay_undrained_shear_strength","category":"ground_stiff_clay","label":"Stiff clay: undrained shear strength s_u","status":"verified","value_si":75000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":50000,"high_si":150000,"display":"s_u ~ 50-100 kPa (US scale 'stiff') or 75-150 kPa (BS 5930:1999 'stiff'; ISO 'high')","sources":[{"title":"BGS OR/15/065 Appendix 2 (BS 5930: Stiff = UCS 0.15-0.3 MPa)","url":"https://earthwise.bgs.ac.uk/index.php/OR/15/065_Appendix_2_-_Strength,_consistency_and_density_classification_terms_and_descriptions"},{"title":"Geocentrix: ISO 14688-2","url":"https://www.geocentrix.co.uk/help/content/references/iso14688/undrained_shear_strength_of_fine_soils.htm"},{"title":"Groundhog docs: strength bands","url":"https://groundhog.readthedocs.io/en/dev/site_investigation/categories.html"}],"notes":"The central 75 kPa (where the two schemes overlap) is my choice. Same undrained traction-cap logic as for soft clay.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_asphalt_allowable_contact_pressure_aviation","category":"ground_asphalt","label":"Asphalt (flexible) pavement: allowable tyre-pressure categories in the pavement rating system","status":"verified","value_si":1750000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":500000,"display":"W unlimited; X <= 1.75 MPa (254 psi); Y <= 1.25 MPa (181 psi); Z <= 0.50 MPa (73 psi)","sources":[{"title":"Fiji CAA AIC 04/25 (ICAO ACR-PCR tyre pressure codes)","url":"https://caaf.org.fj/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/AIC-04-25-CHANGES-TO-PAVEMENT-STRENGTH-CLASSIFICATION-SYSTEM.pdf"},{"title":"Iowa DOT PCR report 2024 (FAA AC 150/5335-5D codes)","url":"https://ia.iowadot.gov/aviation/pavementmanagement/airport-details/docs/pcr-reports/fort-dodge-pcr-report-2024.pdf"}],"notes":"These are serviceability limits for repeated aircraft tyre loads on rated airfield pavements. They are not the ultimate capacity under a single static punch. Ordinary roads are not rated this way. Code W has no limit, so no high_si is given. The value shown is the X limit.","who_when":"ICAO ACR-PCR / FAA AC 150/5335-5D"},{"key":"ground_asphalt_ultimate_bearing_small_punch","category":"ground_asphalt","label":"Asphalt pavement on compacted base: ultimate bearing under a 0.1 m^2 foot","status":"estimate","value_si":2500000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":1000000,"high_si":5000000,"display":"~1-5 MPa (order-of-magnitude estimate)","sources":[{"title":"Context only: tyre-pressure categories (Fiji CAA AIC 04/25)","url":"https://caaf.org.fj/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/AIC-04-25-CHANGES-TO-PAVEMENT-STRENGTH-CLASSIFICATION-SYSTEM.pdf"}],"notes":"Order-of-magnitude estimate only. I found no published ultimate static punch capacity. Reasoning: high-category flexible pavements routinely carry tyre pressures up to 1.75 MPa in service without damage, so the single-load ultimate is higher. The asphalt and base spread the load onto the subgrade, which ultimately governs. Asphalt is viscoelastic, so it is much weaker when hot and under sustained load (rutting) than when cold and under rapid load. Treat the range as very uncertain.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_asphalt_claw_traction_coefficient","category":"ground_asphalt","label":"Asphalt: friction coefficient, keratin scales/claws","status":"estimate","value_si":0.7,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.5,"high_si":0.9,"display":"~0.7 (0.5-0.9) dry","sources":[{"title":"No direct source found (estimate)","url":"https://what-if.xkcd.com/1/"}],"notes":"My estimate; no measured data found. The URL is a placeholder because the schema requires one; it does not support this number. Reasoning: dry asphalt's coarse macrotexture lets claw tips interlock with aggregate, giving roughly rubber-like grip. Wet surfaces would be lower. With very high force, claws plough the binder and the limit becomes asphalt shear failure, for which I found no value.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_concrete_slab_fc","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Concrete slab-on-grade: specified compressive strength f'c","status":"verified","value_si":24130000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":17240000,"high_si":27580000,"display":"17.2 MPa (2,500 psi) interior slabs; 20.7-24.1 MPa (3,000-3,500 psi) exposed garage slabs; 27.6 MPa (4,000 psi) steel-troweled garage option","sources":[{"title":"Minnesota Rules 1309.0402 (IRC Table R402.2 as amended), 2019 version","url":"https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/1309.0402/version/2019-11-13%2011:38:17+00:00"}],"notes":"These are residential minimums (IRC Table R402.2 as adopted in Minnesota). Industrial floors commonly specify higher strengths, but I did not verify a typical industrial value, so high_si stops at 4,000 psi. 1 psi = 6,894.757 Pa.","who_when":"IRC R402.2 (MN-amended, 2019)"},{"key":"ground_concrete_bearing_strength_aci","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Concrete local bearing (crushing) strength per ACI 318","status":"verified","value_si":41000000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":14650000,"high_si":46900000,"display":"B_n = 0.85 f'c A1 sqrt(A2/A1), sqrt(A2/A1) <= 2 (max 1.7 f'c); phi = 0.65","sources":[{"title":"Lecture (ACI 318 bearing check, phi = 0.65, sqrt(A2/A1) <= 2)","url":"https://www.uomus.edu.iq/img/lectures21/MUCLecture_2022_8556371.pdf"}],"notes":"A1 is the loaded area and A2 the geometrically similar supporting area. A foot on a large slab gets the full sqrt(A2/A1) = 2. Value: 1.7 x 24.13 MPa = 41 MPa. Low: 0.85 x 17.24 MPa (no confinement benefit). High: 1.7 x 27.58 MPa. This is a code nominal limit; actual crushing under a confined punch can be higher. In practice the slab punches through or cracks in flexure well before the surface crushes (see next entries). The secondary source cites the ACI 318 bearing clause; I could not open the code text.","who_when":"ACI 318 bearing provisions"},{"key":"ground_concrete_punching_shear_stress_aci","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Concrete two-way (punching) shear stress capacity, ACI 318","status":"verified","value_si":1620000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":1370000,"high_si":1730000,"display":"v_c = 4 lambda sqrt(f'c) psi = 0.33 lambda sqrt(f'c) MPa (smallest of three ACI expressions); critical perimeter b0 at d/2 from the loaded area","sources":[{"title":"StructurePoint: GammaF in two-way slab punching shear (ACI 318-14)","url":"https://structurepoint.org/publication/pdf/The%20Role%20of%20GammaF%20in%20Two-way%20Slab%20Punching%20Shear%20Calculations%20in%20ACI%20318.pdf"}],"notes":"v_c = min(4, 2 + 4/beta, alpha_s*d/b0 + 2) x lambda*sqrt(f'c) psi. Values computed for f'c = 17.24-27.58 MPa (central 24.13 MPa). This is for structural two-way slabs. Plain slabs-on-ground are designed differently (ACI 360, not checked), and subgrade support inside the perimeter adds capacity.","who_when":"ACI 318-14 two-way shear provisions"},{"key":"ground_concrete_slab_on_grade_punch_through_estimate","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Slab-on-grade: average foot pressure to punch through (0.1 m^2 foot)","status":"estimate","value_si":2500000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":2300000,"high_si":8000000,"display":"~2.5 MPa (100 mm residential slab) to ~8 MPa (200 mm, 34 MPa slab)","sources":[{"title":"Formula basis: ACI 318 two-way shear (StructurePoint)","url":"https://structurepoint.org/publication/pdf/The%20Role%20of%20GammaF%20in%20Two-way%20Slab%20Punching%20Shear%20Calculations%20in%20ACI%20318.pdf"}],"notes":"My calculation: V = 0.33*sqrt(f'c)*b0*d, with b0 = 4(B + d), B = 0.316 m and d taken as the slab thickness. Cases: 100 mm at 17-21 MPa gives V ~ 0.23-0.25 MN (about 2.3-2.5 MPa under the foot). 150 mm at 27.6 MPa gives ~0.48 MN. 200 mm at 34.5 MPa gives ~0.80 MN. Caveats: this ignores subgrade reaction (which raises capacity), plain-concrete and reinforcement effects, and flexural cracking (which may come first). After cracking the slab acts as broken plates on the subgrade.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_concrete_claw_traction_coefficient","category":"ground_concrete_slab","label":"Concrete: friction coefficient, keratin scales/claws","status":"estimate","value_si":0.6,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.4,"high_si":0.8,"display":"~0.6 (0.4 smooth/troweled to 0.8 broom-finished)","sources":[{"title":"Context: IBC Table 1806.2 friction coefficients (concrete footing on soil/rock)","url":"https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/ca-building-code/chapter-18-soils-and-foundations/section-1806-presumptive-load-bearing-values-of-soils"}],"notes":"My estimate; no measured data found. Keratin cannot penetrate concrete, so this is surface friction plus claw-tip catching on texture. Steel-troweled slabs are at the low end, broom-finished at the high end.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_granite_ucs","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Intact granite: uniaxial compressive strength (UCS)","status":"verified","value_si":200000000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":100000000,"high_si":300000000,"display":"~100-250+ MPa; fresh granite is an ISRM 'extremely strong' (>250 MPa) example","sources":[{"title":"Hoek, Practical Rock Engineering, Ch. 11, Table 2 (field estimates of UCS)","url":"https://www.rocscience.com/assets/resources/learning/hoek/Practical-Rock-Engineering-Chapter-11-Rock-Mass-Properties.pdf"},{"title":"BGS OR/15/065 Appendix 2 (rock strength classes)","url":"https://earthwise.bgs.ac.uk/index.php/OR/15/065_Appendix_2_-_Strength,_consistency_and_density_classification_terms_and_descriptions"}],"notes":"Hoek's Table 2 classes are R5 Very strong 100-250 MPa (examples include granodiorite and gneiss) and R6 Extremely strong >250 MPa (examples include fresh granite and quartzite). Hoek gives m_i = 32 +/- 3 for granite. Weathered granite is far weaker. The 200 MPa central value and the 300 MPa high end are my choices; 300 MPa is not a hard ceiling.","who_when":"Hoek (Practical Rock Engineering); Brown 1981 grades"},{"key":"ground_granite_bearing_confinement_factor","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Rock under a small punch: ultimate bearing / UCS (confinement factor)","status":"estimate","value_si":8.5,"unit_si":"1","low_si":1,"high_si":13.8,"display":"q_ult ~ (N_phi + 1) x UCS (strip) x 1.25 (square); N_phi = tan^2(45 + phi/2) -> ~8.5-14 for intact rock; lower bound ~1 x UCS","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-2908 Rock Foundations (1994), Eqs 6-2, 6-4, 6-5, 6-7 and Table 6-1","url":"https://www.cedengineering.com/userfiles/Rock%20Foundations-R1.pdf"}],"notes":"Derivation from the EM 1110-1-2908 equations: local-shear q_ult = c*N_c (+ 0.5*gamma*B*N_gamma), with N_c = 2*N_phi^0.5*(N_phi + 1). For intact rock the lower-bound cohesion is c = q_u/(2*tan(45 + phi/2)) (Eq 6-7a, s = 1). Together these give q_ult ~ q_u*(N_phi + 1) for a strip, times 1.25 for a square (Sowers). For an assumed intact friction angle phi = 45-55 deg, N_phi = 5.8-10.1, so the factor is 6.8-11.1 (strip) or 8.5-13.8 (square). The phi range is my assumption, not sourced. Poorly confined, jointed rock columns fail near the unconfined strength (Eq 6-5: 2c*tan(45 + phi/2) = q_u), so the factor drops toward 1. Secondary sources attribute q_ult = q_u(N_phi + 1) to Goodman (1989); I did not open Goodman.","who_when":"Estimate built on USACE EM 1110-1-2908 (30 Nov 1994)"},{"key":"ground_granite_ultimate_bearing_small_punch","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Intact granite: ultimate bearing under a 0.1 m^2 foot","status":"estimate","value_si":1700000000,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":100000000,"high_si":4100000000,"display":"~1.7 GPa (0.1-4 GPa)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-2908","url":"https://www.cedengineering.com/userfiles/Rock%20Foundations-R1.pdf"},{"title":"Hoek Ch. 11","url":"https://www.rocscience.com/assets/resources/learning/hoek/Practical-Rock-Engineering-Chapter-11-Rock-Mass-Properties.pdf"}],"notes":"UCS x confinement factor: 200 MPa x 8.5 = 1.7 GPa. Low: jointed or weathered rock at about its UCS (100 MPa x 1). High: 300 MPa x 13.8. Real outcrops are jointed, and the joints often govern.","who_when":"Estimate, 2026-10"},{"key":"ground_granite_presumptive_allowable","category":"ground_granite_bedrock","label":"Crystalline bedrock (granite): presumptive ALLOWABLE bearing","status":"verified","value_si":7660800,"unit_si":"Pa","low_si":574560,"high_si":7660800,"display":"NAVFAC/USACE massive crystalline rock, hard sound: 160 ksf (7.66 MPa); IBC Class 1 crystalline bedrock 12,000 psf (575 kPa)","sources":[{"title":"USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Table 4-8","url":"https://www.tugraz.at/fileadmin/user_upload/Institute/IAG/Files/18_Bearing_Capacity_of_Soils-USACE.pdf"},{"title":"IBC/CBC Table 1806.2","url":"https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/ca-building-code/chapter-18-soils-and-foundations/section-1806-presumptive-load-bearing-values-of-soils"}],"notes":"ALLOWABLE values. A useful no-suit reference next to the suited 511 kg.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the deadlift world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_deadlift_world_record"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Elephant bar","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elephant_bar"}]},{"key":"powerlifting_deadlift_raw_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Raw powerlifting deadlift, all-time world record (any federation)","status":"verified","value_si":492.5,"unit_si":"kg","display":"492.5 kg (1,085.8 lb)","who_when":"Colton Engelbrecht (South Africa), 11 Jul 2026, WRPF Nikolai Kagansky Memorial Cup, Moscow, Russia (bodyweight 125.3 kg, U140 kg class)","notes":"Federation: WRPF, per OpenPowerlifting. Raw division, so no supportive suit. FitnessVolt notes that lifting straps are forbidden in powerlifting, so this is a hook or mixed grip. Wikipedia records it as a sumo deadlift. Sumo uses a wide stance and shortens bar travel compared with conventional, so ROM is shorter than in strongman pulls. He made it on his 2nd attempt and missed 500 kg. Previous record: Danny Grigsby 487.5 kg (WRPF American Pro, 29 Jul 2022). The sources did not say whether the meet was drug-tested.","sources":[{"title":"OpenPowerlifting: Colton Engelbrecht","url":"https://www.openpowerlifting.org/u/coltonengelbrecht"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Engelbrecht all-time raw total at 2026 Kagansky Cup","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/colton-engelbrecht-all-time-heaviest-raw-total-2026-nikolai-kagansky-memorial-cup/"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: All-time raw deadlift records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/raw-deadlift-men/"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the deadlift world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_deadlift_world_record"}]},{"key":"powerlifting_deadlift_ipf_classic_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"IPF Classic (raw) deadlift open world record, heaviest class","status":"verified","value_si":411,"unit_si":"kg","display":"411.0 kg (906.1 lb)","who_when":"Temur Samkharadze (Georgia), 8 Sep 2024, IPF Sub-Junior & Junior Championships, Malta (120+ kg class)","notes":"Federation: IPF, and this is the heaviest men's open classic deadlift on the IPF/Goodlift records list. Classic means no suit and no straps. It is much lower than the WRPF all-time raw mark (492.5 kg), so the figure the sim uses depends on which federation it takes as human peak. The Goodlift page text was partly obfuscated. Wikipedia's progression table gives the same 411 kg entry.","sources":[{"title":"Goodlift (IPF records): World Open Men's Classic Records","url":"https://www.goodlift.info/records.php?eq=1"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the deadlift world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_deadlift_world_record"}]},{"key":"powerlifting_deadlift_equipped_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Equipped (multi-ply) powerlifting deadlift, heaviest listed","status":"verified","value_si":457.5,"unit_si":"kg","display":"457.5 kg (1,008.6 lb)","who_when":"Andy Bolton (UK), April 2009, BPC South East Championships/Qualifier, Eton, England","notes":"Federation: BPC. Multi-ply equipped. Wikipedia's progression table gives this as the latest equipped entry. Bolton's Wikipedia page calls it a 'former world record' because raw lifts have since gone heavier (Magnusson 460.5 kg raw in 2011; Engelbrecht 492.5 kg raw in 2026). Deadlift suits help far less than squat suits. I could not get a current all-federation multi-ply ranking from OpenPowerlifting to confirm that nothing heavier exists.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Andy Bolton","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Bolton"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the deadlift world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_deadlift_world_record"}]},{"key":"powerlifting_deadlift_ipf_equipped_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"IPF Equipped deadlift open world record, heaviest class","status":"verified","value_si":420,"unit_si":"kg","display":"420.0 kg (925.9 lb)","who_when":"Krzysztof Wierzbicki (Poland), 26 Jul 2017, World Games, Wroclaw, Poland (-120 kg class)","notes":"Federation: IPF. Equipped means a single-ply suit under IPF rules. The 120+ kg class record is lower, at 405.5 kg (Dubai, 23 Nov 2019). Goodlift page text was partly obfuscated, but names, weights and dates match Wikipedia's IPF equipped entry.","sources":[{"title":"Goodlift (IPF records): World Open Men's Equipped Records","url":"https://www.goodlift.info/records.php"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the deadlift world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_deadlift_world_record"}]},{"key":"deadlift_straps_exhibition_engelbrecht","category":"lift_record","label":"Heaviest floor deadlift reported (exhibition, straps, no suit)","status":"claimed","value_si":520,"unit_si":"kg","display":"520 kg (1,146.4 lb)","who_when":"Colton Engelbrecht, 28 Mar 2026, exhibition lift after a WRPF meet in Russia (FitnessVolt calls it the 2026 Siberian Power Show; OpenPowerlifting lists WRPF 'Start 800 Powerlifting Tournament', equipment 'Straps')","notes":"Sumo deadlift with belt and lifting straps, no suit. Done as an extra exhibition pull after his 9 meet attempts. Straps are banned in powerlifting and the stance is not strongman format, so it counts as a record under neither rulebook. It is 9 kg heavier than the official 511 kg strongman record, but sumo ROM is shorter. One outlet (Box Life) questioned the claim. Treat it as an unofficial upper reference.","sources":[{"title":"FitnessVolt: Engelbrecht 520 kg sumo deadlift with straps","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/colton-engelbrecht-520-kg-sumo-deadlift-lifting-straps-2026-siberian-power-show/"},{"title":"OpenPowerlifting: Colton Engelbrecht","url":"https://www.openpowerlifting.org/u/coltonengelbrecht"},{"title":"Box Life: skepticism on 1,146 lb claim","url":"https://boxlifemagazine.com/viral-deadlift-record-claim-skepticism/"}]},{"key":"silver_dollar_deadlift_wr","category":"partial_lift","label":"Silver dollar (18-inch) deadlift world record","status":"verified","value_si":580,"unit_si":"kg","display":"580 kg (1,278.7 lb)","who_when":"Rauno Heinla (Estonia), 4 Jun 2022, Silver Dollar Deadlift Estonian Championship, Viljandi, Estonia","notes":"Partial range. The bar starts about 18 in (0.457 m) off the floor, so the lift is roughly knee-to-lockout. Belt and figure-8 straps. Sources disagree on a suit: FitnessVolt says he 'seems to have used' a deadlift suit, while BarBend says t-shirt, no suit. Previous record: Ben Thompson 577.2 kg (WDC Worlds, Paisley, 7 May 2022). Sean Hayes pulled about 560 kg in Apr 2022. No 2025-2026 record above 580 kg was found. Do not compare it with full-ROM deadlifts.","sources":[{"title":"FitnessVolt: Rauno Heinla 580 kg silver dollar deadlift","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/rauno-heinla-silver-dollar-deadlift-world-record/"},{"title":"BarBend: Rauno Heinla 580 kg silver dollar deadlift","url":"https://barbend.com/news/rauno-heinla-world-record-silver-dollar-deadlift-580-kilograms/"},{"title":"Breaking Muscle: Sean Hayes silver dollar deadlift (18-inch definition)","url":"https://breakingmuscle.com/sean-hayes-silver-dollar-deadlift-world-record-1235-pounds/"}]},{"key":"hummer_tire_deadlift_wr","category":"partial_lift","label":"Hummer tire deadlift world record (elevated partial deadlift)","status":"verified","value_si":549,"unit_si":"kg","display":"549 kg (1,210 lb)","who_when":"Oleksii Novikov (Ukraine), 12 Aug 2022, Shaw Classic, Loveland, Colorado, USA","notes":"Partial range: the bar starts elevated, with Hummer tires as the plates. My sources gave no start height. Belt and straps; Breaking Muscle could not tell whether he wore a suit. Beat JF Caron's 545 kg (2020). No 2025-2026 record was found.","sources":[{"title":"Breaking Muscle: Novikov 1,210 lb Hummer tire deadlift","url":"https://breakingmuscle.com/oleksii-novikov-hummer-tire-deadlift-1210-pounds/"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Max Hummer tire deadlift progression","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/strongman/records/progression/max-hummer-tire-deadlift/"}]},{"key":"trap_bar_deadlift_12in_wr","category":"partial_lift","label":"Trap bar deadlift from 12 inches (joint world record)","status":"verified","value_si":514.5,"unit_si":"kg","display":"514.5 kg (1,134 lb)","who_when":"Lucas Hatton and Evan Singleton (joint), 16 Aug 2025, Strongest Man on Earth (Shaw Classic), Loveland, Colorado, USA","notes":"Partial range: trap bar starting 12 in (0.305 m) off the floor. A different bar and setup from the 511 kg record, so it does not displace that record. Sources are Wikipedia and FitnessVolt, not a sanctioning body.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Lucas Hatton","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Hatton"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: 2025 Strongest Man On Earth results","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/2025-strongest-man-on-earth-results/"}]},{"key":"back_lift_record_ernst","category":"lift_record","label":"Heaviest weight ever lifted by a human (back lift), Guinness","status":"verified","value_si":2422.18,"unit_si":"kg","display":"2,422.18 kg (5,340 lb)","who_when":"Gregg Ernst (Canada), 28 Jul 1993, South Shore Exhibition, Bridgewater, Nova Scotia","notes":"Back lift of a platform holding two cars and their drivers, performed and notarized. A back lift is a tiny-range lift: the lifter braces under a platform resting on trestles and raises it just clear, with the load spread across the back and the legs nearly straight. Guinness gives no lift height. Displacement is very small, so work done is small even though force is huge. Guinness still named Ernst as holder in April 2026. Do not treat it as a full-ROM lift.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest weight ever lifted","url":"http://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/115841-heaviest-weight-ever-lifted"},{"title":"Guinness (Apr 2026): What is the strongest part of the human body","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2026/4/what-is-the-strongest-part-of-the-human-body-these-records-might-surprise-you"}]},{"key":"back_lift_claim_anderson_1957","category":"historical_claim","label":"Paul Anderson claimed back lift","status":"disputed","value_si":2844.02,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":1846.12,"high_si":2844.02,"display":"Claimed 6,270 lb (2,844 kg); historian's reconstruction at most ~4,070 lb (1,846 kg)","who_when":"Paul Anderson (USA), claimed 12 Jun 1957, his backyard, Toccoa, Georgia","notes":"No photos, no video and no written witness accounts. Strength historian Joe Roark (Iron Game History vol. 7 no. 1, June 2001) found the safe on the platform weighed about 1,200 lb less than claimed and the 1,800 lb wooden table was implausible. His generous reconstruction is about 4,070 lb (1,846 kg). Guinness once listed it, then removed it; I did not find the year it was removed. Even the low bound is unverified.","sources":[{"title":"Joe Roark, 'Paul Anderson's June 12, 1957 Backlift', Iron Game History 7(1), 2001","url":"https://www.starkcenter.org/igh/igh-v7/igh-v7-n1/igh0701e.pdf"},{"title":"The Barbell: Most weight ever lifted","url":"https://thebarbell.com/most-weight-ever-lifted/"}]},{"key":"back_lift_claim_cyr","category":"historical_claim","label":"Louis Cyr claimed back lift","status":"claimed","value_si":1967.23,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":1874.7,"high_si":1967.23,"display":"4,337 lb (1,967 kg) per modern retellings; 4,133 lb (1,875 kg) per 1956 Guinness wording","who_when":"Louis Cyr (Canada), reported 1895 (Boston) or 1896 (Chicago)","notes":"Platform said to carry 18 men. No photos. The Canadian Encyclopedia gives Boston 1895 and 1,967 kg. Roark quotes the 1956 Guinness listing as 4,133 lb in Chicago in 1896 (back lift off trestles). The sources disagree on weight, year and city. Historical exhibition, unverified.","sources":[{"title":"The Canadian Encyclopedia: Louis Cyr","url":"https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/article/louis-cyr"},{"title":"Joe Roark, Iron Game History 7(1), 2001 (quotes 1956 Guinness entry)","url":"https://www.starkcenter.org/igh/igh-v7/igh-v7-n1/igh0701e.pdf"},{"title":"The Barbell: Most weight ever lifted","url":"https://thebarbell.com/most-weight-ever-lifted/"}]},{"key":"hip_lift_best","category":"partial_lift","label":"Heaviest hip/harness lift (carousel)","status":"claimed","value_si":1266,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":1150,"high_si":1266,"display":"1,266 kg (2,791 lb) on TV; 1,150 kg joint competition record (2012)","who_when":"Nick Best (USA), History Channel 'The Strongest Man in History' (reported July 2019); competition mark 1,150 kg shared with Mike Jenkins, Giants Live Melbourne 2012","notes":"Hip lift: load hangs from a belt or harness at the hips and is raised only a few cm by straightening the legs. The 1,266 kg lift was a TV stunt on Paul Anderson's carousel, not a sanctioned contest. Eddie Hall said one side stayed on the ground on the first try, and Best repeated it. The 1,150 kg figure is the competition record.","sources":[{"title":"FitnessVolt: Nick Best breaks hip lift record","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/nick-best-break-hip-lift-record"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Nick Best","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Best"},{"title":"The Barbell: Most weight ever lifted","url":"https://thebarbell.com/most-weight-ever-lifted/"}]},{"key":"iwf_category_reset","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"IWF bodyweight-category changes and world-record reset (2025 and 2026)","status":"verified","value_si":0.97,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.97,"high_si":0.98,"display":"New 'World Standards' = 97% (June 2025) / 98% (Aug 2026) of trend from old records","who_when":"IWF; categories effective 1 Jun 2025, revised again effective 1 Aug 2026","notes":"From 1 Jun 2025 the IWF cut to 8 categories per sex. Men: 60, 65, 71, 79, 88, 94 (first announced as 98), 110, +110 kg. All earlier records were frozen as historical. New 'World Standards' were set at about 97% of the old records (fitted with a polynomial regression), and a lifter must beat a standard by at least 1 kg to set a record. From 1 Aug 2026 (LA28 alignment) the men's categories became 60, 65, 70, 75, 85, 95, 110, +110 kg, with new standards at 98% of a trendline. The unchanged categories (men's 60, 65, 110, +110) kept their records. So the heaviest current marks (+110 kg) are post-2025 records, while Talakhadze's heavier lifts are historical. Several IWF pages returned 403 to me, so the 97% figure comes via search summaries and Weightlifting House.","sources":[{"title":"IWF: World Standards established for new IWF bodyweight categories (Jun 2025)","url":"https://iwf.sport/2025/06/26/world-standards-established-for-new-iwf-bodyweight-categories/"},{"title":"ASOIF: IWF establishes World Standards for new bodyweight categories (Aug 2026)","url":"https://www.asoif.com/news/iwf-establishes-world-standards-new-bodyweight-categories"},{"title":"IWF: World standards for the new bodyweight categories (5 Aug 2026)","url":"https://iwf.sport/2026/08/05/iwf-establishes-world-standards-for-the-new-bodyweight-categories/"},{"title":"BarBend: IWF new weightlifting categories June 2025","url":"https://barbend.com/news/iwf-new-weightlifting-categories-june-2025/"},{"title":"Wikipedia: List of world records in Olympic weightlifting","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_Olympic_weightlifting"}]},{"key":"olympic_clean_jerk_current_wr","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"Clean & jerk world record, current categories (men +110 kg)","status":"verified","value_si":261,"unit_si":"kg","display":"261 kg (575.4 lb)","who_when":"Alireza Yousefi (Iran), 17 May 2026, Asian Weightlifting Championships, Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar, India","notes":"First record above the +110 kg World Standard of 260 kg. Full range: floor to overhead, no straps or suits, belt allowed. Yousefi's 262 kg at the 2024 Worlds came under the old +109 kg category, so it is not a current world record. The +110 total record is still the 477 kg World Standard.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: List of world records in Olympic weightlifting","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_Olympic_weightlifting"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Yousefi 261 kg clean & jerk world record","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/alireza-yousefi-sets-clean-jerk-world-record-2026-asian-weightlifting-championship/"},{"title":"Indian Weightlifting Federation report","url":"https://iwlf.in/irans-alireza-yousefi-creates-new-world-asian-records-in-mens-110kg-at-asian-weightlifting-championships-2026/"}]},{"key":"olympic_snatch_current_wr","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"Snatch world record, current categories (men +110 kg)","status":"verified","value_si":219,"unit_si":"kg","display":"219 kg (482.8 lb)","who_when":"Ali Ammar Yasser (Iraq), 29 Sep 2026, Asian Games, Aichi-Nagoya, Japan","notes":"First record above the +110 kg World Standard of 218 kg. Full range: floor to overhead in one motion. He took silver: 465 kg total against Ali Davoudi's 466 kg.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: List of world records in Olympic weightlifting","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_Olympic_weightlifting"},{"title":"Shafaq News: Timing confusion denies Iraqi weightlifter Asian gold","url":"https://shafaq.com/en/sport/Timing-confusion-denies-Iraqi-weightlifter-Asian-gold"}]},{"key":"olympic_clean_jerk_heaviest_ever","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"Heaviest clean & jerk ever (historical record, 2018-2025 categories)","status":"verified","value_si":267,"unit_si":"kg","display":"267 kg (588.6 lb)","who_when":"Lasha Talakhadze (Georgia), 17 Dec 2021, IWF World Championships, Tashkent, Uzbekistan (+109 kg)","notes":"Frozen historical record after the June 2025 category reset. Same meet: 492 kg total. It passed Leonid Taranenko's 266 kg (1988). Full range, no assistive gear beyond belt and wraps.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Lasha Talakhadze","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasha_Talakhadze"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Talakhadze three world records at 2021 Worlds","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/lasha-talakhadze-records-2021-iwf-world-championships/"},{"title":"Wikipedia: List of world records in Olympic weightlifting (historical section)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_Olympic_weightlifting"}]},{"key":"olympic_snatch_heaviest_ever","category":"olympic_weightlifting","label":"Heaviest snatch ever (historical record, 2018-2025 categories)","status":"verified","value_si":225,"unit_si":"kg","display":"225 kg (496 lb)","who_when":"Lasha Talakhadze (Georgia), 17 Dec 2021, IWF World Championships, Tashkent, Uzbekistan (+109 kg)","notes":"Frozen historical record after the June 2025 category reset.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Lasha Talakhadze","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasha_Talakhadze"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Talakhadze three world records at 2021 Worlds","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/lasha-talakhadze-records-2021-iwf-world-championships/"}]},{"key":"log_press_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Log lift (log press) world record","status":"verified","value_si":231,"unit_si":"kg","display":"231 kg (509.26 lb)","who_when":"Cheick 'Iron Biby' Sanou (Burkina Faso), 7 Sep 2024, Strongman Open / World Log Lift Championships, Birmingham, UK","notes":"Guinness-listed. The log is cleaned from the floor and put overhead. The sources did not give rules on leg drive or jerk style. Record history: Savickas 228 kg, Biby 229 kg (2021), 230 kg (2023), 231 kg (2024). Lucas Hatton's 222.3 kg and Jack Osborn's 222 kg (2025) are lower. The 2026 World Log Lift Challenge in Glasgow is on 17 Oct 2026, after today, so recheck after that date.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest log lift (male)","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/760344-heaviest-log-lift-male"},{"title":"Wikipedia: The World Log Lift Championships","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_World_Log_Lift_Championships"},{"title":"Burkina24: Iron Biby at 2026 World Log Lift Challenge","url":"https://burkina24.com/?p=452565"}]},{"key":"atlas_stone_over_bar_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Heaviest Atlas stone over a 48-inch bar","status":"verified","value_si":286,"unit_si":"kg","display":"286 kg (630 lb) over 1.22 m bar","who_when":"Tom Stoltman (Scotland), 23 May 2020, livestreamed record attempt (World's Ultimate Strongman 'Feats of Strength'), his gym in Scotland","notes":"The stone is lifted from the floor over a 4 ft (1.219 m) bar. Exhibition attempt, not a full contest, with Zydrunas Savickas judging remotely. Previous marks: Stoltman 273 kg (Arnold, Mar 2020) and Brian Shaw 254 kg (2017). I found no single-stone Guinness record for men and nothing heavier through 2026, but the source pages are 2020-2023.","sources":[{"title":"BarBend: Tom Stoltman 286 kg Atlas stone world record","url":"https://barbend.com/news/strongman-tom-stoltman-world-record-286kg-atlas-stone/"},{"title":"LiftingStones.org: Atlas Stones records","url":"https://liftingstones.org/articles/atlas-stones"}]},{"key":"squat_raw_sleeves_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Raw squat (sleeves) all-time world record","status":"verified","value_si":490.5,"unit_si":"kg","display":"490.5 kg (1,081.4 lb)","who_when":"Devonte Lewis (USA), 12 Jun 2026, USAPL Raw Nationals, Lombard, Illinois (bodyweight about 213.5 kg, 140+ kg class)","notes":"Federation: USAPL. Belt and knee sleeves only, no wraps or suit, full depth. It passed Ray Williams' 490 kg (2019) by 0.5 kg. His 480 kg (AMP, 30 Aug 2026) and Jesus Olivares' 485 kg (4 Oct 2026, unofficial IPF record) are lower.","sources":[{"title":"OpenPowerlifting: Devonte Lewis","url":"https://www.openpowerlifting.org/u/devontelewis"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the squat world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_squat_world_record"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: All-time raw squat records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/raw-squat-men/"}]},{"key":"squat_raw_wraps_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Raw-with-knee-wraps squat all-time world record","status":"verified","value_si":525,"unit_si":"kg","display":"525 kg (1,157.4 lb)","who_when":"Vlad Alhazov (Israel/Russia), 22 Dec 2018 (BarBend says 23 Dec), WRPF Adrenaline Grand Prix, Minsk, Belarus","notes":"Federation: WRPF. Belt and elastic knee wraps. Wraps store elastic energy out of the hole, so this is assisted compared with sleeves. BarBend noted it beat the single-ply squat record of the time. Dan Bell's 505 kg (24 Apr 2021) is lower. OpenPowerlifting's table for that meet parsed inconsistently on my fetch, so the figure rests on Wikipedia, BarBend and FitnessVolt.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Progression of the squat world record","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progression_of_the_squat_world_record"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Vladislav Alhazov","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladislav_Alhazov"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Wraps squat records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/wraps-squat-men/"}]},{"key":"squat_equipped_wr","category":"lift_record","label":"Equipped (multi-ply) squat, heaviest officially recorded","status":"disputed","value_si":594.66,"unit_si":"kg","low_si":592.3,"high_si":595,"display":"About 595 kg (1,311 lb)","who_when":"Nathan Baptist (USA), 6 Feb 2021, UPA Utah Kick-Off Meet, Clearfield, Utah","notes":"Multi-ply suit plus knee wraps, which is heavily assisted. Three white lights under UPA rules, but depth has been publicly disputed from video. Sources give 594.7 kg (1,311 lb) or 595 kg (OpenPowerlifting rounding). Previous: Brian Carroll 592.3 kg (Oct 2020, RPS). I found no 600 kg squat in 2025-2026, but I could not pull a current multi-ply ranking. Single-ply all-time: 544.3 kg (Rajeev Chandila, 15 Nov 2025, per FitnessVolt).","sources":[{"title":"BarBend: Nathan Baptist 1,311 lb equipped squat","url":"https://barbend.com/powerlifter-nathan-baptist-all-time-world-record-equipped-squat-1311-pounds"},{"title":"Box Life: Contested back squat world record","url":"https://boxlifemagazine.com/contested-back-squat-world-record/"},{"title":"FitnessVolt: Single-ply squat records (men)","url":"https://fitnessvolt.com/powerlifting/records/equipped-squat-men/"}]},{"key":"aircraft_pull_wr","category":"pull_record","label":"Heaviest aircraft pulled by one man (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":188830,"unit_si":"kg","display":"188.83 t (416,299 lb), 8.8 m in 1 min 16 s","who_when":"Rev. Kevin Fast (Canada), 17 Sep 2009, CFB Trenton, Ontario (CC-177 Globemaster III)","notes":"The load is a rolling mass, not a lift. The pulling force only has to beat rolling resistance and inertia, a small fraction of weight, and that force was not measured. The Canadian Press gave 188,694 kg. Guinness's 'Where' field says Cobourg, which conflicts with its own text saying Trenton. Guinness does not describe the rope or harness. Still listed as current.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records: Heaviest aircraft pulled (male)","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/heaviest-aircraft-pulled-by-a-man"},{"title":"IronMind (18 Sep 2009): New Guinness record heaviest aircraft pulled","url":"https://ironmind.com/news/New-Guinness-World-Record-Heaviest-Aircraft-Pulled-by-an-Individual"}]},{"key":"vehicle_pull_100ft_wr","category":"pull_record","label":"Heaviest vehicle pulled over 100 ft by one man (Guinness)","status":"verified","value_si":99060,"unit_si":"kg","display":"99,060 kg (218,389 lb) over 30.48 m","who_when":"Rev. Kevin Fast (Canada), 5 Jul 2017, Cobourg, Ontario","notes":"Rolling pull over a 100 ft (30.48 m) course. The Guinness page does not describe the vehicle(s), time or harness. Guinness credits 'Statcast, which began recording velocities in 2008', but the 2008-2014 system was PITCHf/x, so the label is loose. This is a ball speed near release, not a hand speed. Fastest since: 105.7 mph (Chapman, 2016); 105.5 mph (Ben Joyce, 2024; Jacob Misiorowski, 26-27 Jun 2026, a record for a starter). Wikipedia cites the 2013 Guinness 'Fan Choice' item.","sources":[{"title":"Guinness World Records news (9 Aug 2013): Fan Choice Record, fastest martial arts punch","url":"https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2013/8/fan-choice-record-august-9-50361/"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Keith Liddell","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Liddell"}]},{"key":"punch_fist_speed_elite_measured","category":"biomechanics_endpoint_speed","label":"Elite punch fist speed (lab-measured)","status":"verified","value_si":11.95,"unit_si":"m/s","low_si":6.6,"high_si":12.5,"display":"Peak about 6.6-12.5 m/s; best mean peak 11.95 m/s (lead hook)","who_when":"Whiting, Gregor & Finerman 1988; Piorkowski, Lees & Barton 2011; Stanley et al. 2018","notes":"Whiting et al. 1988 (Am J Sports Med 16(2):130-136, 3D film, experienced boxers): peak fist velocity 6.6-12.5 m/s, reached 8-21 ms before contact; contact velocity 5.9-8.2 m/s. Piorkowski et al. 2011 (10 competition-standard athletes, 8-camera optoelectronic): single maximal contact speed 9.26 +/- 2.09 m/s; hooks faster than jab or cross. They also cite Atha et al. 1985: 8.9 m/s contact for one professional heavyweight (Frank Bruno), and Walilko 2005: 8.16 m/s for amateurs. Stanley et al. 2018 (IJPAS 18:835-854, 15 amateurs): lead hook peak 11.95 +/- 1.84 m/s, the highest punch type. Straight punches are slower: elite lead straight 7.16 m/s (Liu et al. 2022). Karate punches are reported at 10-15 m/s (Feld, McNair & Wilk, Sci Am 1979, via a secondary source only). Peak speed and contact speed differ.","sources":[{"title":"Whiting et al. 1988, Am J Sports Med 16(2):130-136 (record)","url":"https://lida.sport-iat.de/dbv/Record/4039170?lng=en"},{"title":"Piorkowski, Lees & Barton 2011, Single maximal versus combination punch kinematics (accepted manuscript)","url":"https://knowledge.lancashire.ac.uk/3757/1/piorkowski-et-al-2011-punch-kinematics.pdf"},{"title":"Stanley et al. 2018, IJPAS 18(5):835-854","url":"https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/rpanxx/v18y2018i5p835-854.html"},{"title":"Liu et al. 2022, Frontiers in Physiology 13:1015154","url":"https://frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fphys.2022.1015154/full"},{"title":"Science.ca Ask a Scientist (cites Sci Am April 1979 karate article)","url":"https://science.ca/askascientist/viewquestion.php?qID=821"}]},{"key":"standing_vertical_jump_nfl_record","category":"jump_record","label":"Highest standing vertical jump, NFL Scouting Combine record","status":"verified","value_si":1.1684,"unit_si":"m","display":"46 in (1.168 m)","who_when":"Gerald Sensabaugh (North Carolina), 2005 NFL Scouting Combine, Indianapolis","notes":"Measured as jump-and-reach (Vertec): standing reach subtracted from jump reach, with countermovement and arm swing. Combine conditions differ from official standing long jump rules (landing on turf, not sand), so it is not ratified.","sources":[{"title":"Wikipedia: Standing long jump","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_long_jump"},{"title":"SpeedEndurance: Byron Jones standing long jump world record video","url":"https://speedendurance.com/2015/02/23/byron-jones-standing-long-jump-world-record-video/"}]},{"key":"bolt_peak_running_speed","category":"speed_record","label":"Usain Bolt peak running speed (100 m WR race)","status":"verified","value_si":12.42,"unit_si":"m/s","display":"12.42 m/s (44.72 km/h)","who_when":"Usain Bolt (Jamaica), 16 Aug 2009, World Championships 100 m final (9.58 s WR), Berlin","notes":"Average over the fastest 20 m section (60-80 m, 20 m split = 1.61 s), not an instantaneous laser peak. Caution: the Zatsiorsky/de Leva thigh fraction is more than 40% larger (about 0.14) than Dempster's, per the BMClab comparison, so the choice of model matters for kick or stomp momentum.","sources":[{"title":"BMClab data file: BSP Dempster model adapted by Winter (2009)","url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BMClab/BMC/master/data/BSP_DempsterWinter.txt"},{"title":"BMClab notebook: Body segment parameters (Dempster vs Zatsiorsky comparison)","url":"https://nbviewer.org/github/demotu/BMC/blob/master/notebooks/BodySegmentParameters.ipynb"}]},{"key":"segment_mass_fraction_whole_leg","category":"biomechanics_segment","label":"Whole leg (thigh + shank + foot) mass fraction","status":"verified","value_si":0.161,"unit_si":"1","display":"0.161","who_when":"Dempster 1955 via Winter 2009","notes":"Greater trochanter to medial malleolus, including the foot. Equals 0.100 + 0.0465 + 0.0145.","sources":[{"title":"BMClab data file: BSP Dempster model adapted by Winter (2009)","url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BMClab/BMC/master/data/BSP_DempsterWinter.txt"}]},{"key":"hill_force_velocity_equation","category":"biomechanics_muscle","label":"Hill force-velocity equation (form)","status":"verified","display":"(F + a)(v + b) = (F0 + a) b; v = b(F0 - F)/(F + a); vmax = b F0 / a","who_when":"A.V. Hill 1938 (frog sartorius); reviewed by Alcazar et al. 2019, Front Physiol 10:769","notes":"F = force, v = shortening velocity, F0 = maximal isometric force, a has force units and b has velocity units. Curvature is set by a/F0 (equivalently b/vmax): smaller a/F0 means a more curved relation. It applies to concentric (shortening) contractions only. For eccentric loading, force plateaus at about 1.6-2.0 F0 in isolated muscle (Mashima et al. 1972, cited in the same review). Hill's form is empirical.","sources":[{"title":"Alcazar et al. 2019, On the shape of the force-velocity relationship in skeletal muscles, Front Physiol 10:769","url":"https://frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2019.00769/full"}]},{"key":"hill_curvature_a_over_F0","category":"biomechanics_muscle","label":"Hill curvature parameter a/F0","status":"estimate","value_si":0.25,"unit_si":"1","low_si":0.18,"high_si":0.32,"display":"Typical 0.25 (convention); measured about 0.18-0.32 in muscle or single joints","who_when":"Hill 1938; Edman et al. 1976; Martin, Martin & Morlon 1994; Rivière et al. 2023","notes":"0.25 is a widely used normalization value. Lecture notes give a = b = 0.25 when F0 = vmax = 1; it comes from frog data, not a measured human population mean. Values derived from the Alcazar 2019 review: Hill 1938 frog sartorius about 0.20; Abbott & Wilkie 1953 about 0.28; Edman fibres 0.18-0.29. Human in vivo (Martin et al. 1994, Eur J Appl Physiol 69:539-544): best-fit curvature 0.28 for ankle extensors and 0.32 for elbow flexors. Their parameter 'af' controls curvature; I assume it is a/F0 but did not confirm from full text. Whole-limb multi-joint leg press (Rivière et al. 2023, Sports Med Open, 9 athletes): a/F0 from 0.53 to 2.70, i.e. close to linear, and the authors prefer a linear model for multi-joint pushes. a/F0 falls with temperature and is lower (more curved) in slow-twitch muscle. Use about 0.25 for single muscles and expect much flatter curves at whole-limb level.","sources":[{"title":"Alcazar et al. 2019, Front Physiol 10:769","url":"https://frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2019.00769/full"},{"title":"Martin, Martin & Morlon 1994, Eur J Appl Physiol 69(6):539-544 (record)","url":"https://www.bisp-surf.de/Record/PU199501100267"},{"title":"Rivière et al. 2023, Sports Medicine - Open (low force-high velocity domain in lower-limb extensions)","url":"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10344854/"}]},{"key":"pitch_ball_release_speed_professional","category":"biomechanics_endpoint_speed","label":"Professional pitcher ball release speed (typical, lab-measured)","status":"verified","value_si":37,"unit_si":"m/s","low_si":33,"high_si":47.3,"display":"About 37 m/s typical pro (about 83 mph); about 47.3 m/s record","who_when":"Fleisig et al. 1999 (J Biomech 32:1371-1375), as cited in Kageyama et al. 2014 (J Sports Sci Med 13:742-750)","notes":"Professional mean 37.0 m/s (Fleisig 1999); university pitchers 33-35 m/s across several studies; collegiate high-velocity group 37.4 m/s. Hand speed at release is roughly ball speed. The high bound is Chapman's 105.8 mph record. I only saw Fleisig's per-level figures through a secondary citation.","sources":[{"title":"Kageyama et al. 2014, J Sports Sci Med 13(4):742-750","url":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4234942"},{"title":"Fleisig et al. 1999, J Biomech 32(12):1371-1375 (record)","url":"https://sponet.de/sponet/Record/4005289"}]},{"key":"kick_foot_speed_soccer","category":"biomechanics_endpoint_speed","label":"Soccer full-instep kick foot speed before ball contact","status":"verified","value_si":21.6,"unit_si":"m/s","display":"21.6 m/s (pass kick 18.3 m/s)","who_when":"Levanon & Dapena 1998, Med Sci Sports Exerc 30(6):917-927","notes":"Knee extension produced about 86% of foot speed in the full kick. Ball speed is higher than foot speed because of the light ball and restitution; pro ball speeds of 22-30 m/s are reported elsewhere.","sources":[{"title":"Levanon & Dapena 1998, MSSE 30(6):917-927 (record)","url":"https://www.bisp-surf.de/Record/PU199807303122"}]},{"key":"kick_foot_speed_taekwondo","category":"biomechanics_endpoint_speed","label":"Taekwondo roundhouse kick peak linear foot velocity","status":"verified","value_si":17.36,"unit_si":"m/s","low_si":16.53,"high_si":17.36,"display":"Elite 17.36 +/- 0.70 m/s; sub-elite 16.53 +/- 1.35 m/s","who_when":"Moreira et al. 2021, PLoS One 16(6):e0235582 (14 black belts)","notes":"Bandal chagi (roundhouse) only. A moving-target study (Straiotto et al. 2021) reports lower mean foot segment velocities of 13.6 m/s elite and 11.4 m/s non-elite, which is a different measure.","sources":[{"title":"Moreira et al. 2021, PLoS One","url":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8189470/"}]},{"key":"vertical_jump_takeoff_velocity_elite","category":"biomechanics_endpoint_speed","label":"Vertical takeoff velocity of centre of mass, elite jumpers","status":"estimate","value_si":4.79,"unit_si":"m/s","low_si":4.5,"high_si":4.84,"display":"About 4.5-4.8 m/s","who_when":"Derived: v = sqrt(2 g h) with h = 1.1684 m (Sensabaugh 46 in) gives 4.79 m/s; Helene & Yamashita 2005 high-jump model gives 4.5 m/s","notes":"No peer-reviewed measured value for elite takeoff vertical velocity was retrieved, so this is a physics estimate (g = 9.80665 m/s^2). The 4.5 m/s figure is a model output for a running high jump with a 7.5 m/s approach, not a measurement. I did not read the primary Clark & Weyand text.","sources":[{"title":"Scientific American (Aug 2016): The secret to human speed","url":"https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/the-secret-to-human-speed"},{"title":"Coh et al. 2018, Kinesiology 50(2):172-180","url":"https://ojs.srce.hr/kinesiology/article/view/5579"},{"title":"Coh 2019, Facta Universitatis PES 17(1):1-13","url":"https://casopisi.junis.ni.ac.rs/index.php/FUPhysEdSport/article/download/4984/3002"},{"title":"NASE: Force, motion and speed (summarizes Clark & Weyand 2014)","url":"https://www.naseinc.com/blog/force-motion-and-speed/"}]},{"key":"foot_plantar_contact_area_standing","category":"biomechanics_contact_area","label":"Barefoot plantar contact area of one adult foot, quiet standing","status":"verified","value_si":0.007966,"unit_si":"m^2","low_si":0.007072,"high_si":0.009525,"display":"About 71-95 cm^2 per foot (static); about 112-140 cm^2 per foot during walking stance","who_when":"Kang et al. 2024 (J Korean Foot Ankle Soc 28(1):21-26); Kuruma et al. 2023 (World Physiotherapy Congress abstract)","notes":"Kang 2024, healthy normal feet, static barefoot standing, per foot: EMED-n50 79.66 +/- 11.82 cm^2; HR Mat 70.72 +/- 13.80 cm^2. Dynamic total contact was 139.96 and 111.85 cm^2. Kuruma 2023 (30 young adults, SR Soft Vision): 190.5 +/- 30.6 cm^2 for both feet, i.e. about 95 cm^2 per foot. Contact area depends on the sensor threshold and the device. Weight shifted onto one foot, or the forefoot in push-off, changes it.","sources":[{"title":"Kang et al. 2024, Comparative Analysis of Two Pedobarography Systems, J Korean Foot Ankle Soc","url":"https://synapse.koreamed.org/articles/1516086755"},{"title":"Kuruma et al. 2023, Effect of foot band on foot alignment in standing posture (World Physiotherapy Congress)","url":"https://world.physio/congress-proceeding/effect-foot-band-foot-alignment-standing-posture"}]},{"key":"palm_contact_area_adult","category":"biomechanics_contact_area","label":"Palm area of one adult hand","status":"verified","value_si":0.0077853,"unit_si":"m^2","low_si":0.0073659,"high_si":0.01465,"display":"Palm about 74-78 cm^2; whole palmar hand incl. fingers about 132-147 cm^2","who_when":"Agarwal & Sahu 2010, Indian J Plast Surg 43(1):49-53 (300 adults, hand tracing)","notes":"Adult means: male palm 77.853 +/- 10.29 cm^2, female palm 73.659 +/- 9.14 cm^2. Whole hand including digits: male 146.5 cm^2, female 132.4 cm^2. The population is small-bodied (mean BSA 1.59 m^2 male, 1.44 m^2 female). As ratios, palm is about 0.50% of body surface area and hand about 0.92%, so scale up for larger bodies. This is traced outline area. Actual contact area when pressing a flat surface is smaller because of the hollow palm. The high bound is the whole palmar hand, not the palm alone.","sources":[{"title":"Agarwal & Sahu 2010, Determination of hand and palm area as a ratio of body surface area in Indian population","url":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2938623/"}]}]

RESEARCHER GAPS:
["The OpenPowerlifting all-time rankings filtered to multi-ply did not load. So it is not confirmed that Andy Bolton's 457.5 kg (2009) is still the heaviest equipped powerlifting deadlift, or that Nathan Baptist's about 595 kg is still the heaviest equipped squat. Both rest on the Wikipedia progression tables and news reports.","The federation for Colton Engelbrecht's 492.5 kg raw deadlift comes from OpenPowerlifting (WRPF). No source said whether the meet was drug-tested, so the sim should not assume it was.","The IWF's own pages returned HTTP 403. The 2025 '97%' World Standard rule and the Aug 2026 category list come from IWF and ASOIF search summaries, Wikipedia and secondary outlets. The 219 kg snatch and 261 kg clean & jerk were checked against Wikipedia and news, not the IWF records page.","The World Athletics records page did not render. The throw records were checked through Wikipedia plus 2026 news and previews. A record set late in the 2026 season and not covered by those pages cannot be fully ruled out.","I did not retrieve the official 2009 Berlin biomechanics report (Graubner & Nixdorf 2011). Bolt's 12.42 m/s comes from Coh 2019, whose abstract contradicts its own table about Zagreb. No instantaneous laser peak speed was verified.","I did not read the primary Clark & Weyand 2014 text. The about 5.0 x body-weight peak force comes from secondary reports (Scientific American, SMU, NASE).","No peer-reviewed measured takeoff vertical velocity for elite jumpers was found, so that entry is a physics estimate.","No authoritative population mean for the human Hill curvature a/F0 was found. 0.25 is a normalization convention from frog data. Whether the 'af' in Martin et al. 1994 equals a/F0 was not confirmed from full text. I could not read the text of Wilkie (1949/1950) on human elbow flexors.","The method behind the Guinness 'fastest martial arts punch' (Keith Liddell, 45 mph) is undocumented. The karate fist speeds of 10-15 m/s (Feld, McNair & Wilk, Scientific American 1979) and Atha 1985 (8.9 m/s) were seen only through secondary citations.","Fleisig 1999's per-level ball velocities were seen only as cited by Kageyama 2014.","No current Guinness single-stone record for men was found. Tom Stoltman's 286 kg over a 48 in bar (May 2020) is not confirmed as still standing in 2026, though nothing heavier turned up.","The start height for the Hummer tire deadlift is not documented in the sources found. Whether Rauno Heinla wore a suit for the 580 kg silver dollar deadlift is disputed between sources.","No Guinness record page was found for the 2025 Cairo train pull by teeth. AP's '279 tons' does not say which ton.","Guinness gives no hold time or body position for the 2,000 kg weight-sustained record, and no harness method for the aircraft and vehicle pulls. No pulling forces were measured for any pull record, so the sim must model rolling resistance itself.","The year Guinness removed Paul Anderson's 1957 back-lift claim was not found. The year, city and weight of Louis Cyr's back lift differ between sources (1895 Boston 4,337 lb vs 1896 Chicago 4,133 lb).","Nick Best's 1,266 kg hip lift was a TV production with no stated sanctioning or judging. The exact filming date was not found (the article is from July 2019).","The 2026 World Log Lift Challenge (Glasgow, 17 Oct 2026) happens after today's date and could change the 231 kg log record.","The claimed 47.1 in vertical jump by Josh Imatorbhebhe (2015, jump mat) and Willie Creear's 47 in regional-combine jump were not verified and were left out of the facts.","Static plantar contact area depends on the device and sensor threshold. No single normative adult value exists, so the foot entry is a range across two devices and studies. Palm area comes from one small-bodied population (mean body surface area 1.59 m^2 for males) and needs scaling."]

Conceptcarz lists S-3 weights of 3,040 lb (general), 3,150 lb (Touring Sedan) and up to 3,540 lb (LWB Limousine), so the value is the touring sedan and the range spans the listed S-3 weights. AD","notes":"On Prometheus' advice Heracles 'took over the sphere' from Atlas, then tricked Atlas into taking it back while he put a cushion on his head. No mass is given. I found no Heracles feat with a stated quantity. The Augean stables (river diversion) and other labours are unquantified too.","sources":[{"title":"Theoi: Atlas (quoting Apollodorus, trans. Aldrich)","url":"https://www.theoi.com/Titan/TitanAtlas.html"}]},{"key":"thor_utgarda_loki_cat","category":"myth_legend","label":"Thor tries to lift Utgarda-Loki's cat (the Midgard Serpent)","status":"not_quantified","unit_si":"kg","display":"Lifted it until one paw left the floor; the cat was the World Serpent","who_when":"Snorri Sturluson, Prose Edda, Gylfaginning ch. So high didst thou stretch up thine arms that it was then but a little way more to heaven.' Chapter numbers follow Brodeur, and other translations may number differently. It is a count, not a mass. No mass or distance is given.","sources":[{"title":"Bible Gateway: Judges 16 (KJV)","url":"https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Judges+16%3A1-31&version=KJV"}]},{"key":"ruyi_jingu_bang_mass","category":"myth_legend","label":"Sun Wukong's staff (Ruyi Jingu Bang): stated weight","status":"canon_stated","value_si":7965,"low_si":6750,"high_si":8057.016,"unit_si":"kg","display":"13,500 jin, about 7.97 t at the Ming jin of 590 g","who_when":"Journey to the West, chapter 3 (Ming dynasty novel, 16th c.)","notes":"Chapter 3 inscription: '如意金箍棒，重一萬三千五百斤' (Compliant Golden-Hooped Rod, weight 13,500 jin). The text also reads '如意金箍棒，一萬三千五百斤', and the staff is the '天河定底神珍鐵'. Conversion: Wikipedia, citing Elvin (2004), gives the Ming jin as 590 g, so 13,500 x 0.590 = 7,965 kg (Wikipedia rounds to 7,960 kg / 17,550 lb). low_si uses the modern 500 g market jin (6,750 kg), which is anachronistic. high_si uses the 1915 ROC 16-liang jin of 596.816 g (8,057 kg). Anthony Yu's English translation renders the unit as 'pounds', which would understate it. Size in the text: about as thick as a dou measure and more than two zhang long. I did not convert that because the Ming chi length is unsourced here.","sources":[{"title":"Wikisource: 西遊記 第003回 (Chinese text)","url":"https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/西遊記/第003回"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Ruyi Jingu Bang","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruyi_Jingu_Bang"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Chinese units of measurement (jin by dynasty)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_units_of_measurement"}]},{"key":"milo_of_croton_bull","category":"myth_legend","label":"Milo of Croton carries a four-year-old bull around the course at Olympia","status":"not_quantified","unit_si":"kg","display":"No mass stated","who_when":"Athenaeus, Deipnosophistae 10.412e-f (c. AD 200), citing Theodorus of Hierapolis; Yonge translation 1854","notes":"Yonge: 'And once at Olympia he took a four year old bull on his shoulders, and carried it all round the course; and after that he killed it and cut it up, and ate it all up by himself in one day.' Athenaeus also gives variants (Phylarchus has it eaten before an altar; the Dorieus epigram calls it a heifer). Written about 700 years after Milo (fl. late 6th c. BC), so it is legend. No ancient mass is given, and I found no sourced live-weight estimate for an archaic Greek four-year-old bull.","sources":[{"title":"Perseids: Athenaeus Book 10 (Yonge)","url":"https://cts.perseids.org/read/greekLit/tlg0008/tlg001/perseus-eng2/10.0-10.19"},{"title":"Wikipedia: Milo of Croton","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milo_of_Croton"}]},{"key":"milo_of_croton_calf_training","category":"myth_legend","label":"Milo's progressive-overload calf story","status":"not_quantified","unit_si":"kg","display":"Carried a calf daily until it was a bull","who_when":"Quintilian, Institutio Oratoria 1.9.5 (c. AD 95), Butler translation","notes":"'Milo, having accustomed himself to carrying a calf every day, ended by carrying it when grown to a bull.' The Perseids segment spans 1.9.5-1.10.3, and 1.9.5 is the usual citation. No masses or times are given.","sources":[{"title":"Perseids: Quintilian, Institutio Oratoria 1.9.5ff","url":"https://cts.perseids.org/read/latinLit/phi1002/phi001/perseus-eng2/1.9.5-1.10.3"}]}]

RESEARCHER GAPS:
["Marvel handbooks: I found no explicit definition of 'ton' (short, long or metric) in the Deluxe, Master Edition or 2004-era text I searched. Short tons are an inference.","Master Edition (1990-93) per-character ratings for Thor, Hercules, Gladiator, Thing, She-Hulk, Colossus, Spider-Man, Captain America, Wolverine and Luke Cage were not confirmed. Only the Hulk sheet and the strength key were read.","Which characters a later handbook moved to 'Incalculable' (Master Edition) or to power-grid Strength 7 (2004+) was not confirmed for Thor, Hercules, Gladiator or Sentry.","Thing and She-Hulk: no later handbook change from 85 and 75+ tons was confirmed. The 2004 Avengers She-Hulk entry I searched has no tonnage line.","Colossus 'exactly 100 tons' (2008 OHOTMU A-Z) rests on Looper alone and was not found in primary text.","The 2007 Spider-Man '20 tons' profile: the specific handbook or one-shot that first printed it is unidentified (found appended to a scan labelled ASM #544).","The Deluxe Edition 'Strength Level chart' that Deluxe #20 (Feb 1988) refers to: I did not find which issue printed it or its full contents.","Wolverine's 1987 Deluxe #14 entry was not directly confirmed (the 2004 X-Men text was).","Secret Wars #4 (1984): exact verbatim wording, speaker (Reed Richards per Screen Rant), page and panel of the 150-billion-ton statement could not be verified from a scan. 'Spans two miles' is a Screen Rant claim.","All-Star Superman: the page and panel of the '200 quintillion tons' test in #1 (Jan 2006) and its exact wording ('equivalent of'?) could not be verified. The brief's attribution to #3 appears wrong.","Superman vol. 3 #13 (2012): exact dialogue for the Earth-weight bench press, including whether 'six sextillion metric tonnes' is the comic's own wording, could not be verified.","Superman #220 'more force than a million H-bombs': year, page and wording unverified (Looper only).","Thor and the Midgard Serpent in Marvel comics: no in-universe stated mass or force found for any Thor/Serpent feat (including Thor #380, 1987).","No DC or Marvel stated mass was found for Superman moving the Moon (Superman IV is a film with no figure) or for pre-Crisis planet-towing (e.g., Superboy #140, 1967).","Hercules towing Manhattan (Marvel Team-Up #28, Dec 1974): no stated mass. Hulk #241 retcons it. Any Manhattan mass would be the sim's own estimate.","Milo of Croton: no sourced live-mass estimate for an archaic Greek four-year-old bull was found.","Ruyi Jingu Bang dimensions (about a dou thick, over two zhang long) were not converted because I did not source a Ming chi/zhang length.","Action Comics #1 car: the make is an informed guess (1937 DeSoto, possibly Plymouth or Dodge). I could not open the Plymouth P4 weight page directly, and the cover car differs from the interior-panel car.","Hulk 'Antarctica, 30 quadrillion U.S. tons' (Screen Rant): whether the comic states the number, and its issue and year, are unverified."]

The Deluxe #2 entry the researcher cites goes on to give a number: 'While not superhuman, he is as strong as a human can be. He can lift (press) a maximum of 800 pounds'. The claims 'no tonnage given' and 'popular figures such as 800 lb did not turn up in any handbook text' are false. Status should be canon_stated, value 800 lb = 362.873896 kg (a maximum). Averaging uses Cauchy's result that a convex body's mean projected area is surface area / 4, which gives (LW+LH+WH)/2 for a box. Dimensions: length 8 ft 11-3/4 in (2.74 m), width 61-3/4 in (1.56 m; header says 157 cm), height ~1 m (not verified). Rim: single bent rim of 17 layers of hard rock maple. Plate: cast grey iron. Grip material: maple rim, crushing strength parallel to grain ~54 MPa (mat_hard_maple). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~0.44 to 0.49 MPa, well below maple's crushing strength, so the gripped spot holds. But the case, legs, lyre and the string-tensioned plate are joined by glue and bolts not designed for single-point lifting, and their strength is not quantified. Expect legs or joints to fail before the rim crushes. The high end is a heavy tourer (CVO Street Glide, 838 lb running order, 380 kg; the standard Street Glide is 811 lb wet, 368 kg, 2.41 x 0.975 x 1.35 m). Grip material: steel or aluminium frame. The MT-07 frame material is not listed on Yamaha's spec page. Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~0.18 MPa on the MT-07. Lifting by the main frame is fine. Bolt-on parts (handlebars, pegs, fairings, mirrors) are not designed for the bike's weight and would bend or snap off (not quantified). I did not reach toyota.com or the Toyota pressroom. Dimensions: 182.3 in L (4.630 m), 70.1 in W (1.781 m, KBB), 56.5 in H (1.435 m, dealer listings), wheelbase 106.3 in. Grip material: mostly mild/drawing-quality sheet steel body panels (DC04-class yield 140 to 210 MPa, mat_dc04_mild_steel) plus higher-strength steels in pillars and sills (not quantified). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~1.3 MPa, about 1% of sheet yield in pure bearing. But body panels are thin and work only as part of the welded shell, so a hand-sized grip on a door or fender pulls the panel out of plane and dents or tears it locally (not quantified). Grip on a sill, pillar or suspension mount to lift the car intact. I did not open the primary handbook. The upper value assumes the GDLS quote means short tons (78 short tons = 70,760 kg), but the quote does not specify the ton. For comparison, SEPv2 is 71.2 short tons (64.6 t). Dimensions (Abrams family): length 9.77 m gun forward, 7.93 m hull; width 3.66 m; height 2.44 m. Grip material: composite armour, including depleted-uranium layers on the M1A2, over steel (rolled homogeneous armour, hardness classes 260 to 470 HB, mat_rha). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~65 MPa, well under armour-steel strength. The welded hull is a stiff box, so a hull lift should hold. Tracks, road wheels and external stowage would hang or tear off. Drag: tumbling box Cd ~1.0 to 1.3.","who_when":"ASA(ALT) 2018 handbook via Wikipedia; Breaking Defense Sept 2023"},{"key":"abrams_projected_area","category":"object_area","label":"Abrams projected area (hull bounding box)","value_si":28.7,"low_si":8.93,"high_si":29,"unit_si":"m^2","display":"~9 (front) to 29 m^2","status":"estimate","sources":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M1_Abrams","title":"Wikipedia - M1 Abrams dimensions"}],"notes":"Box 7.93 x 3.66 x 2.44 m (hull length; overall height; gun excluded). Most masses come from length regressions or piecemeal weighing (Lockyer 1976). NOAA Fisheries: North Atlantic/North Pacific animals reach ~90 ft (27 m) and over 100,000 lb; Antarctic animals reach ~110 ft (33.5 m) and over 330,000 lb (149.7 t). Typical length ~26 m (NOAA PMEL). Grip material: skin and blubber over muscle; tissue strength not quantified. Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~98 MPa, about half the compressive strength of cortical bone and far above any plausible soft-tissue strength. A hand would sink into the animal rather than lift it. Out of water, a whale's body is not built to carry its own weight from one point (not quantified). Other workers (Paul & Larramendi 2025) argue for lower ceilings around 200 t, so treat heavier figures as disputed models, not records. Grip stress at 1 g is ~186 MPa. The 66,000 ton figure is a myth that came from early advertising. Gross register tonnage (46,328 GRT) is a volume measure, not mass. Displacement is the mass of ship plus everything aboard at that draught. Dimensions: length 882 ft 9 in (269.06 m), beam 92 ft 6 in (28.19 m), draught 34 ft 7 in (10.54 m), waterline to boat deck 60 ft 6 in (18.44 m). Grip material: riveted mild-steel hull plate (~193 MPa yield, mat_titanic_hull_steel). Structural note: grip stress at 1 g is ~52 GPa. Even a perfect grip just tears out the plate. A ship is designed to be supported by distributed buoyancy, and out of water a single-point lift breaks the hull girder.
